387YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Hahnmark, Holberg, Karsk, Mareave, Mournwold, Reikos, Segura and the Barrens. The Senate appointed ambassadors, the Imperial Spymaster Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo and generals of seven armies, among other posts. The Synod chose figures such as the Lepidean Librarian Hazelelponi (330 votes) and the Cardinals of Ambition and Vigilance. The Military Council named Giovanni von Temeschwar Imperial Fleet Master and Sibylla Strategos of Dawn. Conclave orders chose grandmasters and Ibiss Briarheart declared for Archmage of Spring. Bourse auctions and votes allocated titles including Master of the Imperial Mint and the Tassatan Hills, won by Serafina di Sarvos with 1103 votes.

n.Dawn: Lady Gwendoloena de Sarroi was elected Senator for the Barrens, and Sibylla was appointed Strategos of Dawn by the Military Council.
n.Grendel: Pathfinder Gaddak was elected to represent Mareave in the Senate.
n.Highguard: Cyrus was elected Senator for Reikos.
n.The Brass Coast: Velasco i Guerra was elected to speak for Segura in the Senate.
n.The League: Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg.
n.The Marches: Simon "Chordwangler" Willow was elected Senator for the Mournwold.
n.Varushka: Sirka Parakgoosier Bashnya was elected Senator for Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Runa was elected to represent Hahnmark in the Senate.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's Senate seat went to Runa at this summit's national election.
t.Holberg: Holberg elected Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg as its senator.
t.Karsk: Karsk returned Sirka Parakgoosier Bashnya as its senator.
t.Mareave: Mareave's senatorial election was won by Pathfinder Gaddak.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold chose Simon "Chordwangler" Willow as its senator.
t.Reikos: Reikos elected Cyrus to its Senate seat.
t.Segura: Segura's senator for the coming term is Velasco i Guerra.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens elected Lady Gwendoloena de Sarroi as their senator.

387YE Spring Equinox Military Council or.d: The Jotun had overrun almost all of Bregasland, but Imperial heroes held the Sallow Way and saved Ottery, for now. A raid on Grismont Township in Reinos failed and the armies withdrew from the hills. Seven armies then marched on Liathaven, which the Jotun have remade as Ashvale. Nine armies and sixteen thousand Summer knights converged on Sarangrave, six of them through the Barrens. The Tusks fought on in the Chalkdowns, and the Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains moved to tame Madruga. In Therunin the vallorn stirred against the Lord Rain ward. Only the Autumn Hammers and Northern Eagle drew the guerdon.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky, Gryphon's Pride and Lions of Adelmar left Astolat to attack Sarangrave alongside Summer knights. The Golden Sun stayed in Astolat on solid defence, its general warning against the self-styled Earl of Groves.
n.Druj: The Druj faced a pincer invasion of Sarangrave by nine Imperial armies. Their great host in Therunin may stay or move as the vallorn stirs there.
n.Grendel: The Grendel still held Mora's Rock. The fate of the Imperial campaign in Madruga was said to depend heavily on where their armada is.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were narrowly denied Ottery after conquering most of Bregasland. They now face seven Imperial armies in Liathaven and the Tusks' continued fighting in Mournwold, though they held Grismont Township in Reinos.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns withdrew to resupply at Virtue's Rest in Bastion while the Quiet Step joined the Sarangrave invasion. Seven armies marched to reclaim Liathaven, once Navarr land.
n.The Brass Coast: The Burning Falcon made a triumphant charge into Madruga and the Fire of the South reinforced Tassato. The Red Wind Corsairs billeted in Mitwold as their general prepared to step down.
n.The League: The Towerjacks dug in at Morrow to help build a citadel in Peregro, and the Wolves of War gave ground there to prepare for the next season.
n.The Marches: The Bounders and Drakes joined the conquest of Liathaven and the Tusks pressed on in the Chalkdowns. The Strong Reeds lay low in Bregasland as Ottery clung on.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard marched in Sarangrave to raise a glass labyrinth around the Druj while letting their subjects slip to safety.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe pressed on to take land in Sarangrave and the Northern Eagle joined the attack there. The Northern Eagle's supporters were granted a share of the guerdon.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear marched into Liathaven against the Jotun, while the Fist of the Mountains began a steady conquest of Madruga.

t.Astolat: The Golden Sun held Astolat on solid defence, while five armies marched out towards Sarangrave and the Wolves of War and Fire of the South departed.
t.Bastion: The Navarr Black Thorns arrived to resupply and reposition at Virtue's Rest.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the shores of the Bay are named among the places of coming chaos, and the Grendel armada's position is a concern.
t.Bregasland: The Jotun held almost all of Bregasland, but heroes kept Ottery, the Otterway and the Sallow Way Imperial for now. The Strong Reeds lay low there.
t.Casinea: The Valiant Pegasus and Summer Storm took up solid defence in Casinea to rest and resupply.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as remaining in command of Mora's Rock; no Imperial army was sent there.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs' general recalls having kept watch on Kahraman.
t.Liathaven: Seven Imperial armies descended on Jotun-held Liathaven, now Ashvale, to break the barbarian hold. Among them, the Autumn Hammers moved to storm the fort in Liath's Glen.
t.Madruga: The Burning Falcon charged into Madruga and the Fist of the Mountains began a steady conquest, seeking to tame the transfigured territory.
t.Mitwold: The Red Wind Corsairs billeted in Mitwold, and the Otterway into Mitwold remained in Imperial hands.
t.Morrow: The Towerjacks dug in to help build a citadel, while the Wolves of War gave ground there to make ready for the next season.
t.Mournwold: The Tusks continued a steady conquest against the Jotun warbands. Farstrider's Watch remained a hall of Jotun champions.
t.Reikos: The Black Thorns and Quiet Step marched out of Reikos, bound for Bastion and Sarangrave respectively.
t.Reinos: An Imperial strike on Grismont Township failed when the orcs held it. The Imperial armies withdrew from the Lasambrian Hills, though some warbands may remain.
t.Sarangrave: Nine Imperial armies and sixteen thousand Summer knights launched a pincer invasion, three continuing in the south and six striking the northern borders.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm seeks to learn more of an ancestor discovered in Skallahn, and the Corsairs recall a foray there.
t.Tassato: The Fire of the South marched swiftly to reinforce Tassato with a solid defence, while the Burning Falcon and Red Wind Corsairs departed.
t.The Barrens: Six armies smashed through the Barrens into northern Sarangrave, and the Gryphon's Pride general called it a land starting to heal.
t.Therunin: The vallorn began to rouse across the Druj-held forests, held back only by the Lord Rain ward. A great Druj host there might stay or move.
t.Upwold: The Valiant Pegasus, Seventh Wave, Green Shield and Narwhal's Spear left Upwold, bound for Casinea and Liathaven.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Jotun warbands picked their way east out of the North Fens as they pressed to finish the conquest of Bregasland.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Ottery held, thanks to heroes who beat the Bounds at Sal-Ott meet and roused the Marcher army. The town will fall if the Jotun keep advancing.
r.Morrow/Peregro: The Towerjacks were ordered to put their engineering skills to helping their friends in Peregro build a citadel.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Tusks marched in steady conquest to reclaim the Chalkdowns, home of their former general Stanley of Chalkdown.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks were told not to advance into Greensward, leaving it as work for the Summer.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: The strike on Grismont Township was meant to break Lasambrian control of Bastasor but failed when the orcs held the town. The captured Faraden trader perished in the fighting.

387YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: Administrative motions created the Synod judgement of Exaltation and the Singer of the Silence, and amended the Apothecaries Guild and Keeper of the Breadbasket. The Senate raised the third Navarr army in Hercynia, the second Urizen army (the Argent Sword) in Redoubt and a fourth Highborn army in Casinea. It ratified the Rahvin and Thule treaties, though a Synod veto of the latter was announced. The Declaration of Remorse and the Toadstone failed. Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo became Imperial Spymaster and built a smugglers cove in Ayereed. Commissions included a Jotun meeting hall on Gull Island and a wayhouse in Ossium. The treasury stood at 1287 thrones and 6 crowns.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish memorial garden in Weirwater honouring the Sweetglade Massacre dead was commissioned then abrogated, the Castle of Thorns throne room restoration was withdrawn, and a memorial hospital was built in Winterbourne, Astolat.
n.Druj: The Senate commissioned an appraisal of how to disrupt Druj operations and resupply in the Forest of Ulnak, with results due before the Summer Solstice 387YE.
n.Highguard: A fourth Highborn army was raised in Casinea, a Steward of the Ossuary title was created for the Grand Ossuary, and the generals of the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus received artefacts as regalia.
n.Imperial Orcs: A dolmen was built in Skymark so the Hylje can return the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell defending Sermersuaq, to be collected by the orcs for proper funerary care.
n.Jotun: The Senate commissioned a feasting hall on Gull Island, Kallavesa, as a new diplomatic meeting place between the Empire and the Jotun, built jointly with Jotun contributions.
n.Navarr: A third Navarr army was commissioned to muster in Treji, Hercynia, and a wayhouse in Ossium was approved to house refugees from Therunin and help fund the Navarr army.
n.Thule: The Senate ratified a treaty with the Thule of Otkodov and appointed an ambassador to them, but a Synod veto of the treaty was to be sought at the Summer Solstice.
n.Urizen: The second Urizen army, the Argent Sword, was raised in Redoubt, and the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade sinecure was built with a title appointed by the Urizen Assembly.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark citizens Finn Pridetalker and Kindra Surefoot became ambassadors to the Commonwealth and Otkodov; Lumi's Legacy was built in Sermersuaq, while the Toadstone fane in Kallavesa failed.

t.Sarangrave: The Imperial Spymaster formally decommissioned the Imperial spy network in Sarangrave, which the Druj had already destroyed a year earlier.

387YE Spring Equinox Synod judgements.d: The General Assembly rejected removing the Doctrine of the Creator (120-952). Viviane Barossa's mandate warning against malign spiritual presences defeated Fintan Nighthaven's rival call to explore them. Corey Wayfarer's mandate to put destroying the vallorn above all else failed. A statement urging the Empire to defeat the Druj before turning on the vallorn passed overwhelmingly. The Synod pledged not to preach to the Thule while Kindra Surefoot's treaty stands. General Rhisiart Dancewalker of the Black Thorns was revoked. Alberto Acciai and Eleanor Novarion were recognised as exemplars of Loyalty and Pride. The Council of Nine set the Silent Bell to investigate the Falconer's cult of the Claw.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly refused to give up a Dawnish fifth army to win the Thule's peace terms (354-0). It praised Dame Katelyn Cordraco, condemned mass spells in tourneys, debated the Earl of the Groves, and narrowly backed returning goods taken from the Rahvin.
n.Druj: The Synod backed defeating the Druj before turning on the vallorn. The Navarr Assembly called for resistance and sabotage against Druj occupation in Therunin, and Druj who fled into Dark Ranging were marked for hunting.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly charged its newly raised fourth army to bring salvation, not hatred. It enacted a mandate of peerless kinship to support other nations, rejected a call to crusade until the last war is won, and warned its Necropolis chapters against cults of the Wastewalker.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly challenged the Synod to prove that exorcising orc ghosts does not destroy their one chance to cross the Abyss. It warned of an old terror rising in the Bay of Catazar and named Sunstorm Nirrin for recognition by all Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: The Marcher Assembly vowed to fight on with General Stanley to drive the Jotun from the Mourn. It praised the Marcher orcs who took up arms against the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr's assembly urged resistance in Therunin, championed Thornsong House and potioncraft, and rallied the nation behind the City of Dreams in Seren. Its general, Rhisiart Dancewalker of the Black Thorns, was revoked by the General Assembly over losses in Therunin.
n.The League: The League Assembly backed building trading posts across Temeschwar and urged citizens of Sarvos and Apulian to keep lights burning after the last lighthouse on the Bay of Catazar fell. It also rewarded Gabrieli di Tassato and Novella di Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly pledged to keep fighting until the Mourn is free and honoured the Marcher orcs who fought the Jotun. It recognised Navarr's loyalty and enacted a mandate letting Marcher fleets support the Red Wind Corsairs.
n.Thule: The General Assembly pledged not to preach to the Thule while Ambassador Kindra Surefoot's treaty stands. Dawn rejected the Thule's latest demand for Imperial land, calling it blackmail.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly praised the Ashen Flame coven's defence of Redoubt and supported saving Solen's Doubt's library as the dam rises. It warned Redoubt's coastal people of a winter eternal and asked the Citadel Guard to bring salvation rather than curses to Sarangrave.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly backed its new army and enacted wards to protect the Apstrus dam from restless spirits. It set the Kestov a penance to help rebuild Ossium, warned of Webwood creatures on Ossium's borders, and condemned idolatrous Bone Serpent shrines.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's assembly backed a fane to Sadogua to protect Kallavesa and added Kaisa Denmother to the Chronicle of Heroism. It enacted a mandate shielding Wintermark from mandates without a greater majority, and warned against the cult of the Claw and two Blood on Snow cultists fleeing to Hahnmark.

t.Brocéliande: The Navarr Assembly urged military captains reinforcing the Broch to hunt down the Druj who fled into Brocéliande, aided by heralds of Yaw'nagrah.
t.Casinea: Highguard's fourth army was being raised in Casinea, and the Highborn Assembly charged it to bring salvation rather than mere conquest.
t.Miaren: The Navarr Assembly urged the nation to finish the City of Dreams in Seren before the great work lapses, recalling the Cold Sun's destruction of Rhonwen's Falls.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: donations to the Synod's Virtue Fund were received at the counting house of Reikos.
t.Sarangrave: The Ambition Assembly urged help for Sarangrave's oppressed septs to explore the Way. The Urizen Assembly asked the Military Council to summon Irra Hara's Wooden Fastness there instead of targeting curses through the Citadel Guard.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: donations to the Synod's Virtue Fund were received at the counting house of Semmerholm.
t.Tassato: The League Assembly narrowly called on Tassato's citizens to recognise Gabrieli di Tassato as rightful challenger to Gabriel Barossa's legacy. Donations to the Virtue Fund were also received at Tassato's counting house.
t.Upwold: Two Blood on Snow cultists behind a recent attack in Upwold were reported fleeing north to Hahnmark. Upwold's senator was praised for voting against road tolls.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Dark Ranging was named as the refuge of Druj who fled there with heralds of Yaw'nagrah, and Imperial captains were urged to search it.
r.Casinea/Woodwych: Mentioned in passing: Destin of the Woodwych Harts raised a Vigilance judgement supporting the pilgrimage of the hallowed coronation bells.

387YE Spring Equinox event schedule.d: Eight nations held senatorial elections in their camps on Saturday afternoon: the Marches for Mournwold, Varushka for Karsk, the Brass Coast for Segura, Highguard for Reikos, Wintermark for Hahnmark, the Imperial Orcs for Mareave, Dawn for the Barrens and the League for Holberg. Six nations elected national titles by Tally of the Votes. The timetable included Senate, Military Council, Conclave and Synod sessions with their deadlines, battles off Anvil on Saturday and Sunday mornings, the Bourse auction and Grandmaster elections, militia meetings, and gatherings such as the Imperial Economics Conference. It also included a vote of Urizen magicians on an offer from the Thule.

n.Dawn: Dawn elected the senator for the Barrens at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney, and Dawnish fleet captains met in the Military Council tent on Saturday.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the schedule, though the Mareave senatorial election appears under the Imperial Orcs.
n.Highguard: Highguard began its inquisition of candidates for the Reikos senator at 2:00pm and elected the Bursar of the House of Spirits at the Chapel at 3:30pm.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs elected the senator for Mareave from 2:15pm, with candidates presenting items of worth. At the Fire Pit at 4:00pm they also elected the Steel Fist, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post and the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast began its auction for the Segura senator at 2:00pm and elected the Cerevado Nets and the Dhomiro of Afar at the Waypoint at 3:30pm.
n.The League: The League elected the Holberg senator at 3:30pm through a presentation of collected bonds, then elected the Tassatan Hills title and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild at the Plaza at 4:30pm.
n.The Marches: Marcher landowners gathered at 1:30pm to elect the senator for the Mournwold.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the schedule listed a vote of Urizen magicians on an offer from the Thule.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians held a meeting in the Hall of Worlds on Friday evening and a vote on an offer from the Thule on Saturday afternoon.
n.Varushka: Varushka began questioning candidates for the Karsk senator at 1:45pm and elected the Gift of the Dwindling Star, the Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore and the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks at the Central Hearth at 4:00pm.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark set out jars for thirty minutes from 2:00pm to elect the Hahnmark senator, and elected the Mediator of Wreck, the Talon of Kauppahall and the Mediator of Fisk at the Tree of Names at 4:30pm.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator was elected by Wintermark at 2:00pm with jars placed down for thirty minutes. The page notes the next regular election for the seat falls at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.
t.Holberg: Holberg's senator was chosen by the League at 3:30pm through a presentation of collected bonds.
t.Karsk: Varushka elected Karsk's senator, with questioning of candidates beginning at 1:45pm.
t.Mareave: An election for Mareave's senator was listed under the Imperial Orcs at 2:15pm, with candidates presenting items of worth.
t.Mournwold: The Marches elected the Mournwold's senator when the landowners gathered at 1:30pm.
t.Reikos: Highguard elected the senator for Reikos, beginning with an inquisition of candidates at 2:00pm.
t.Segura: The Brass Coast held an auction from 2:00pm to choose Segura's senator.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs elected the Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting by Tally of the Votes.
t.The Barrens: Dawn elected the senator for the Barrens at 2:30pm, immediately after the tourney.

387YE Spring Equinox interlude.d: The Senate set the Imperial Guerdon at 150 thrones, shared only by units supporting the Golden Axe in Sarangrave and the Summer Storm in Reinos. Military units could explore the flood-transformed southern Madruga. Priests were offered four lectures: supporting, studying or watching the Solokha effort, or preaching Prosperity in the Sarcophan Delves. The Blood Red Roads and the White Roads became toll roads, ending their benefits to citizens. Enchantments and curses fell on Redoubt, Feroz, Karov, Necropolis, Kallavesa and all of Dawn. Rivers of Life covered Mournwold, Kahraman and the Barrens. The Penumbral Veil remained over every Imperial territory except Casinea and Mournwold.

n.Dawn: All of Dawn was enchanted with Summer magic that eased Summer creatures' passage and gave everyone there a fascination with showy magic. The Barrens gained Rivers of Life, and all four Dawnish territories lay under the Penumbral Veil.
n.Druj: Navarr warbands raiding the Druj gained a production bonus using rafts the Druj themselves had prepared. Imperial units fighting the Druj with the Golden Axe in Sarangrave earned Guerdon shares.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Axos remained annoyed about Imperial involvement in the failure of its joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon.
n.Highguard: The White Roads became toll roads and no longer benefited Highborn citizens. The Virtues of Autumn coven shielded Necropolis with the Hand of the Dhomiro, and Casinea alone was left outside the Penumbral Veil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Mareave and Skarsind were listed among the territories under the Penumbral Veil.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: units supporting the Imperial army Summer Storm in Reinos, a territory Jotun held, received Guerdon shares.
n.Navarr: Navarr warbands raiding the Druj gained a production bonus after Neala Blackhawk's rescue of an orc treetender. Navarr could also move resources to the Barrens for free thanks to the Last Battle wayhouse.
n.The Brass Coast: Imperial units could explore the reshaped southern Madruga, and the Freeborn coven The Sails of the First Flame wove Rivers of Life over Kahraman. The Sunset Roads kept their usual benefits.
n.The League: The Senate adopted Else von Temeschwar's proposal to turn the Blood Red Roads and White Roads into toll roads. All five League cities lay under the Penumbral Veil, Sarvos most strongly of all.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms blessed with Blessing of New Spring could yield black Shinemoon mushrooms, and Mournwold received Rivers of Life. Marcher fleets gained a bonus trading at Caitun.
n.Urizen: Redoubt was battered by Spring curses yet protected by the Ashen Flame's Pillars of Adamant. Urizen congregations were barred from the Support and Watch Solokha lectures but could Study Solokha.
n.Varushka: The Lyktan coven's Hammers of Fury sped a new army's mustering in Karov, and the Iron and Crow Roads kept their benefits. Varushkan congregations could only take the Study Solokha option among the Solokha lectures.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark fleets escorting the fisherfolk of Westerhal suffered a penalty after Kjellen Saltmire's expedition was driven off by coral husks. Kallavesa was enchanted with a Night feast, and Wintermark fleets gained a bonus at Caitun.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat was listed under the Penumbral Veil and cited as an example of a move that would still cost the usual fee.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion was listed among the Highborn territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the growing influence of the eternal Siakha over the bay was said to make the curses on Redoubt unpredictable.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland was listed among the Marcher territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Casinea: Casinea was the only Imperial territory exempt from the Penumbral Veil, a specificity suggesting dozens of deliberate castings.
t.Feroz: Feroz was again enchanted with Regrow the Land's Heart, healing war scars, aiding fertility and favouring the briar lineage. It also lay under the Penumbral Veil as reclaimed Brass Coast land.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark was listed among the Wintermark territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia was listed among the Navarr territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed among the League cities under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Kahraman: The Sails of the First Flame wove Rivers of Life over Kahraman, reducing army casualties and filling its waters with restorative Spring power.
t.Kallavesa: A Night enchantment filled Kallavesa with vivid dreams of feasting, encouraging people to create and share fine food, drink and company until the Spring Equinox.
t.Karov: The Hammers of Fury sped the mustering of a new Imperial army in Karov. Its mines lost two ingots each but gained a pawn of Autumn vis.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk was listed among the Varushkan territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Madruga: Imperial military units could take the Explore the Southern Reaches venture in the flood-transformed south of Madruga, earning herbs and Adversity Vis until the Spring Equinox.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Mareave was listed as an Imperial Orc territory under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren was listed among the Navarr territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova was listed among the Varushkan territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold was listed among the Marcher territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow was listed among the Urizen territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the failed Axou and Grendel venture into the Mountains of the Moon was still souring Axos trade with the Empire.
t.Mournwold: Rivers of Life were cast over Mournwold, reducing army casualties and healing wounds. It was one of the few territories exempt from the Penumbral Veil.
t.Necropolis: The Hand of the Dhomiro protected Necropolis's coast and tombs from raiders. Personal resources there could not be harmed by plundering armies this season.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was listed among the Varushkan territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt was cursed with storms costing its fleets two ranks and its farms and businesses 72 rings. Meanwhile the Pillars of Adamant shielded its structures and fortifications from damage.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos was listed among the Highborn territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Reinos: Military units supporting the Summer Storm in Reinos were one of only two groups to share the Imperial Guerdon.
t.Sarangrave: Units supporting the Golden Axe in Sarangrave shared the Imperial Guerdon. Navarr warbands raiding the Druj gained a bonus from recovered Druj rafts.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos lay under the Penumbral Veil, and the shroud there was more than three times as powerful as elsewhere.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura was listed among the Brass Coast territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm was listed among the Dawnish territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq was listed among the Wintermark territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind was listed as an Imperial Orc territory under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral was listed among the League cities under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was listed among the League cities under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar was listed under the Penumbral Veil, and the toll-road proposal came from Else von Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: Rivers of Life were cast over the Barrens. Navarr could move resources there for free thanks to the new Last Battle wayhouse, counting as Therunin for voting.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Navarr with resources in the Barrens counted as being in Therunin for senatorial and similar elections.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold was listed among the Marcher territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz was listed among the Varushkan territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater was listed among the Dawnish territories under the Penumbral Veil.
t.Zenith: Koboldi from Zenith, servants of the King Under the Mountain, travelled to Redoubt to examine the Pillars of Adamant. Zenith itself lay under the Penumbral Veil.

r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Last Battle wayhouse, completed in the Bleaks as a reconnaissance base against the vallorn, let Navarr take resources in the Barrens for free this season.

387YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Emperor Vesna addressed the Empire about Therunin. Appraisals covered destroying the Jotun Kongegőr bridge and resettling displaced Varushkans around Delev. Diplomatic winds addressed the Commonwealth, Thule, Sarcophan Delves, Faraden, Axos, Asavea and Sumaah, and the Iron Confederacy, Grendel and Jotun. Other winds dealt with Dawn's Summer enchantment and new army, Marcher cattle markets and freed smiths, Spiral's troubles and a proposed dam on the Doubt, and an Autumn offer concerning Urizen. Further notes reported the Rahvin taking Bitter Strand, road tolls raising Senate income by one hundred thrones, Spring storms on Redoubt, Hammers of Fury in Karov and Big Icebarn hunting in the Suaq Wastes. A table recorded the results of twenty-eight conjunctions.

n.Dawn: A Summer enchantment over Astolat, Semmerholm, Weirwater and the Barrens drew boons from Summer heralds, and Senator Éamon Ashenmourn de Cordraco must name the new army mustering in Astolat. Debate also continued over the manticore Earl of the Groves, and Morrigan Mortére was asked to host the Charnel Lord's envoy.
n.Druj: The Druj kept the Barrow Axe and the standard of Isaella's Dance after two Eastring conjunctions went untaken. They survived Imperial attacks in Grimfen Mire and Beladrarsh but lost most of their force at the Splintering Jetty.
n.Grendel: The Shuttered Lantern laid the groundwork for a Regario Dossier office in the Grendel-held settlement of Vorlach, and the Grendel figured in the Keep Talking diplomacy. Imperial attacks on the Grendel in Icarion and on Maistir Varden in Ayereed both ended in retreat.
n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly and Benefactors' Council faced choices in A Peerless Sacrifice, and the Hand of the Dhomiro reduced crime in Necropolis. Tolls were imposed on the White Roads, and Jack Flint of Highguard led as Field Marshal at Visten Head.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs were tagged as interested parties in the new Marcher cattle markets, the plan to dam the Doubt to relieve Icarion in Mareave, and the eternals' plenipotentiary responses.
n.Jotun: An appraisal set out how the Kongegőr between Skallahn and Hordalant might be destroyed to hamper Jotun cooperation. In the Mournwold, Jarl Haakon was killed with honour, though the Jotun prevailed in Halbera Strongarm's challenge.
n.Navarr: Navarr settled in the Barrens shared in Dawn's Summer enchantment, and the Rahvin sept took Bitter Strand and the Fangs, provisionally accepting a treaty. In Therunin a treetender was rescued, and Navarr were among those whose acceptance of Yaw'nagrah's boons the Silent Bell investigated.
n.The Brass Coast: The Silver Chalice's plans for a grand lodge, the Well of Life, were completed for Madruga, where mage-killers were also routed. Spring magic touched Feroz and Kahraman, and the Strategos protected the Celesti Lighthouse and claimed a fleet.
n.The League: The Archbishop of Capodomus preached an inspiring sermon in Sarvos, where a dire astacid and wreckers were defeated at Charoko. League interests also featured in Spiral's troubles and in Holberg's dealings with Faraden and the Delves.
n.The Marches: The freed Marcher smiths were ready to share their lost art, and the new cattle markets produced 818 cattle bonds. The Husks of the Deep still threatened the Gullet coast, Jarl Haakon fell in the Mournwold, and the Silent Bell investigated Marchers who accepted Yaw'nagrah's boons.
n.Thule: With the peace treaty with Otkodov due to expire after the Summer Solstice, negotiations were under way, and the Archmage of Autumn invited the City of Gold and Lead to make trade more appealing to the dragons. The Mediator of Wreck also sought to soothe the Thule of Volham.
n.Urizen: The Silver Flame offered a trade ministry in Cinion, or failing that foci for Urizen's senators, while the City of Lead and Gold made a remarkable offer concerning the nation. Spring storms hit Redoubt's fleets, farms and businesses, though the Pillars of Adamant protected its great works.
n.Varushka: Naomi of Virtue's Rest presented proposals for resettling displaced Varushkans around Delev, and the Hammers of Fury sped the mustering of an army in Karov. The Charnel Lord sought a meeting on military arrangements with Varushka, and odd disappearances were reported in the east.
n.Wintermark: More than ten thousand strength of Winterfolk joined Big Icebarn's hunt in the Suaq Wastes, and it will stay if at least three thousand support it next season. Enchanted feasts were reported in Kallavesa, and Wintermark heroes took on threats at West Marsh, Stark and East Floes.

t.Astolat: A new Dawnish army was being mustered here, awaiting its name and quality from the Senator for Astolat, and the territory shared in the Summer enchantment that drew boons from Summer heralds.
t.Ayereed: An attempt led by the Imperial Spymaster to kill Maistir Varden at Saoirse's Fields ended in Imperial retreat.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Keep Talking diplomacy wind on the Iron Confederacy, Jotun and Grendel was labelled with the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: The Roost's Reeve's conjunction at the Swollen Fens took casualties and was driven off by the husks from the Gullet, though the warnings it prompted have helped contain the danger.
t.Brocéliande: The Knight of the Greenwood recovered all the chests at the Broken Stand.
t.Feroz: Regrow the Land's Heart continued its gentle rains here, soothing those caught in the fighting at Oran but achieving little else, while the Celesti Lighthouse was protected and a fleet claimed.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Champion of Prosperity's attack on the Druj at the Crimson Boscage suffered casualties and left the Druj alive.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: listed among the north-western territories touched by a wave of violence in the Stars and Sigils wind.
t.Hercynia: The Spear of the Seven stopped a horde at the Shattered Pines, and the territory was named among those affected by violence sweeping the north-west.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Holberg Chamber of Commerce, Holbergers and the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market were tagged in the Faraden, Sarcophan and cattle-market winds.
t.Hordalant: An appraisal examined destroying the Kongegőr, the land bridge linking Hordalant to Skallahn, to disrupt Jotun cooperation.
t.Kahraman: The Rivers of Life flowed here, healing injuries swiftly but boosting the growth of weeds, pests and predators as much as crops and livestock.
t.Kallavesa: Enchanted feasts were reported here, Kjellen Saltmire's force was driven off by the husks in the Forlorn Bogs, and the trouble at Redshal Grove remained uncertain.
t.Karov: The Hammers of Fury sped the mustering of a new army here, though each mine produced two fewer ingots and gained a pawn of Autumn vis in their place.
t.Madruga: The Silver Chalice's plans for the Well of Life grand lodge were completed here, partly to help those displaced by the flooding of the Scorrero, and mage-killers were routed at Larroc Corral.
t.Mareave: New cattle markets were established at Stockland and Wayford, and a dam on the Doubt was proposed to relieve Icarion's aridity. An attack on the Grendel ended in retreat, and the fate of the crew at the Salt Shaker remained uncertain.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: northern Miaren was listed among areas affected by the north-western violence in Stars and Sigils.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the earlier revocation of Hal Talbot as Senator for Mitwold was recalled in the Loyalty Assembly's statement.
t.Morrow: Senator Sejanus of the Scarlet Guard may request a realm-focused foci from the Silver Flame if their trade ministry is not commissioned.
t.Mournwold: The Rivers of Life brought indiscriminate fertility here, and Jarl Haakon was killed with honour, though the Jotun won Halbera Strongarm's challenge and the herbalist at the Walters' Clearing was not rescued.
t.Necropolis: The Hand of the Dhomiro protected personal wealth here; no raids came, and theft declined, though thieves also found it easier to evade capture.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: people from Ossium, especially volhov and wardens, were tagged as interested in the Stars and Sigils wind.
t.Otkodov: Negotiations were under way to extend the peace with the Thule of Otkodov before it expires after the Summer Solstice, with Autumn heralds invited to make trade more appealing to the dragons.
t.Redoubt: Spring storms and a Thunderous Deluge struck here, imposing a two-rank fleet penalty and costing farms and businesses 72 rings, though the Pillars of Adamant protected great works. Wreckers were killed at Oathspawned Copse, and timbers of the Astral Phoenix were recovered at Visten Head.
t.Reikos: Ghosts were dealt with at the High Arboretum by Alessi of the Basilisks of the Labyrinth.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden were said to be excited about the invasion of Reinos.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Lady Laudine du Lac's attack on the Druj at the Drained Woods suffered casualties and the Druj survived.
t.Sarvos: The Archbishop of Capodomus preached an inspiring sermon at the newly consecrated cathedral, and a dire astacid and wreckers were defeated at the Grove of Charoko.
t.Semmerholm: The territory was among those under the lingering Summer enchantment that drew boons from almost every Summer eternal interested in the Empire.
t.Sermersuaq: Big Icebarn hunted the monsters of the Suaq Wastes with strong Winterfolk support, the injured at the Screaming Mammoth were helped, and the effort to soothe the Thule of Volham had an unclear result.
t.Shayeel: The Shuttered Lantern prepared the ground for a Regario Dossier office in Vorlach, Shayeel's wealthiest settlement, though a Senate motion is still required.
t.Skallahn: An appraisal examined destroying the Kongegőr, the land bridge linking Skallahn to Hordalant, to hamper the Jotun kingdoms of Kalsea and Narkyst.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: listed among the north-western territories touched by the wave of violence in Stars and Sigils.
t.Spiral: Spiral faced a proposed dam in Apstrus, strange dramaturgical effects in Apulian and Vigilant reports on three threats. The Silver Flame offered a market in Cinion, the Block was protected and the Spire of Black Glass was killed in Screed.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: listed among areas affected by the north-western violence, and home to the accountant Else Van Temeschwar who proposed the road tolls.
t.The Barrens: The Rahvin took Bitter Strand and the Fangs, raising hopes of peace, and the Earl of the Groves courted minor Dawnish houses here. The Barrens also shared in the Summer enchantment and the Rivers of Life, and survivors of Therunin were treated at the Bleaks.
t.Therunin: The Emperor addressed the Empire about Therunin. Two Eastring conjunctions went untaken, leaving Druj trophies in their hands, while a treetender was rescued and most Druj killed at the Splintering Jetty.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, and touched only by Marches-wide matters such as the cattle markets and the freed smiths.
t.Volodmartz: The effort to find and help the Chosen of Samkǒma in the Woods of the Quiet Road had an uncertain outcome.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was under the lingering Dawnish Summer enchantment that drew heralds' boons, and was named among areas affected by the north-western violence.
t.Zenith: Senator Herminius of the House of the Wanderer may request a realm-focused foci from the Silver Flame if their trade ministry is not commissioned.

r.Ayereed/Petrified Forest: The Imperial Spymaster's attempt to kill Maistir Varden at Saoirse's Fields ended in Imperial retreat.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Roost's Reeve's conjunction at the Swollen Fens suffered casualties against the husks of the deep and was driven off, though it uncovered their weaknesses.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: All the chests at the Broken Stand were recovered by the Knight of the Greenwood.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Strategos of the Brass Coast protected the Celesti Lighthouse at Rahab's Orchard and claimed a fleet.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Grimfen Mire: An attack on the Druj at the Crimson Boscage brought Imperial casualties, and the Druj survived.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: The Spear of the Seven stopped a horde at the Shattered Pines.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market was tagged in the cattle-market wind.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: The investigation into what is wrong with the farmers of Redshal Grove had an uncertain result, which the Keeper of the Iron Grove may know more about.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Kjellen Saltmire's force was driven off by the husks in the Forlorn Bogs, though it learned of their weaknesses.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Sakari Nightscale's force routed the mage-killers at Larroc Corral.
r.Mareave/Icarion: A dam on the Doubt was proposed to relieve Icarion's aridity, and an attack on the Grendel at the Plains of the Courath ended in retreat.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: The effort to ensure the safety of the crew at the Salt Shaker had an uncertain result, known perhaps to the Senator for Mareave.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Bryce the Hare's attempt to rescue a herbalist from the Yegarra at the Walters' Clearing failed, with Imperial casualties.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Jarl Haakon was killed with honour at Old Tam Shaffer's Farm and his spoils claimed, but the Jotun won Halbera Strongarm's challenge at Big Boar's Sty.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: one of the traitors slain at Visten Head was named Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: At Visten Head, three timbers of the Astral Phoenix were recovered and one traitor slain, but the Jaws of Selachan remained with the wreckers.
r.Redoubt/Ventosi: Halkyon of the Myriad Stream's force killed the wreckers at Oathspawned Copse and recovered their loot.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Ghosts at the High Arboretum were dealt with.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Beladrarsh: Lady Laudine du Lac's attack at the Drained Woods suffered casualties and the Druj survived.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The Mayor of Caricomare's force defeated a dire astacid and wreckers to protect the people of Charoko.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Mediator of Wreck's attempt to soothe the Thule of Volham at Crow's Rest had an unclear outcome.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The injured at the Wreck of the Screaming Mammoth were helped and the dead laid to rest.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Big Icebarn hunted the monsters of the wastes, backed by over ten thousand strength of Winterfolk, and will remain if at least three thousand support it.
r.Spiral/Ankra: The Urizeni rebels in Ankra were among the three threats in Spiral investigated by the Vigilant.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: A dam was proposed on the Doubt here, which would turn parts of eastern Spiral into a sizeable reservoir.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Silver Flame offered a mithril-columned market here and the title of Architect of Cinion, Urizeni rebels were reported here, and the Block was protected at the Valley of Loss.
r.Spiral/Screed: The malign presence at the heart of Screed remained the obvious threat, but the Spire of Black Glass was killed at Marco's Pass.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin took control of Bitter Strand and its mithril mine, and the Earl of the Groves courted minor Dawnish houses here.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The manticore Earl of the Groves reached out to minor Dawnish houses here, speaking of glory and Ambition.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Survivors of Therunin were treated and counselled at the Last Battle Wayhouse, and bandits threatening the baggage train were defeated at the Golden Thicket.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: Neala Blackhawk's force rescued a treetender at the Splintering Jetty and killed most of the Druj.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Neither conjunction here was taken, so the Barrow Axe and the standard of Isaella's Dance remained with the Druj, while the Krollthorned remained a threat.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The search for the Chosen of Samkǒma in the Woods of the Quiet Road had an uncertain outcome.

387YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Druj overran Therunin's Tarn Valley and entered Peakedge Song, while the Ghulai of the Tainted Basilisk woke the vallorn of Tharunind. Four armies attacked the Sarangrave from Lustri and won, but have no beachhead yet. Grendel land-troops ended the Imperial presence in Ayereed. The Grendel of Mora's Rock helped repel a Children of Wrecks raid on Oran in Feroz. In the Marches, the Ore Hills were freed, but a Jotun host from Liathaven took nearly all of Bregasland. Five armies invaded Reinos and took Ribeira and most of Bastasor. Battle opportunities were offered in Bregasland, Reinos and the Sarangrave. Conjunctions included threats from wreckers, bandits and cultists.

n.Dawn: Dawnish forces readied themselves in Astolat with a force weight of 61, and the Barrens offered conjunctions to exorcise tortured souls and to attend the Earl of the Groves' tournament. Border patrols there mean the Druj need 25 victory points to claim a beachhead.
n.Druj: The Druj overran Therunin's Tarn Valley and pushed into Peakedge Song, and their Ghulai woke the vallorn of Tharunind. In the Sarangrave, though, their resting armies were disrupted and defeated by four Imperial armies.
n.Grendel: Grendel land-troops drove the Empire out of Ayereed and regained the southern borders of Mareave. The Mora's Rock garrison under Commander Fiersach helped turn back the Children of Wrecks at Oran, out of hatred for the wreckers.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies spent the season in Reikos preparing for the year ahead, and Highguard was listed with a force weight of 26 for the coming battles.
n.Imperial Orcs: In Skarsind, cultists of the Claw stole wains of white granite bound for the Brilliant Shore and fled for Pakaanan's Pass, and a conjunction offered a bargain with Tuki of the Little Bones. The nation was listed with a force weight of 5.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost the Ore Hills in Mournwold but swept across Bregasland from Liathaven, leaving only Otterly in Marcher hands. In Reinos they lost Ribeira and almost all of Bastasor, while the Lasambrians refused to surrender.
n.Navarr: Imperial armies withdrew from Therunin, leaving the Druj to conquer the Tarn Valley and assault Peakedge Song, where defenders and the Tarnfather's blessings preserved the ancient houses of healing. Several conjunctions in Therunin were offered to the Navarr, who were listed with a force weight of 58.
n.The Brass Coast: The Children of Wrecks raided Oran in Feroz, and the raid was repelled only with Grendel help. Five armies marched out of Segura into Reinos, and Burnish hosted conjunctions to name constellations.
n.The League: League armies prepared in Tassato, where wreckers guided by the traitor Maurizia Spada di Sarvos threatened to curse the territory. Conjunctions were also offered in Sarvos, Spiral and Holberg.
n.The Marches: Two armies freed the Ore Hills of Mournwold, but the Jotun overran Bregasland despite the Strong Reeds, leaving only Otterly in Marcher hands. Yegarra also threatened Meade March in Mitwold.
n.Urizen: Four armies passed through Lustri into the Sarangrave, wreckers under Tuomas of Pirenea looted ilium in Zenith, and the Ward of the Black Waste was to be performed in Altis. Border patrols mean the Druj need 25 victory points to claim a beachhead in Morrow or Zenith.
n.Varushka: Wreckers serving the traitor Zavetta Voglanova landed in Bittershore and headed to pillage Marshstand Skerry, and the Cabalist of the Hollow Stone was called to stop them. Patrols in Ossium make a Druj beachhead harder.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesa faced bandits threatening Salagiin traders and yegarra raids, and offered a meeting with the ghodi, while a body awaited investigation in Stark. Wintermark was listed with a force weight of 61.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Astolat readied themselves for the year to come.
t.Ayereed: The Imperial beachhead in the petrified forest ended when Grendel land-troops swept in, and soldiers who did not retreat were slain or captured.
t.Bay of Catazar: Defences around the Bay were bolstered against seaborne invasion, while the Empire lost Ayereed and Grendel help repelled a wrecker raid on Feroz.
t.Bregasland: A Jotun host from Liathaven swept across the fens, and despite the Strong Reeds only the town of Otterly remained in Marcher hands. A battle opportunity and conjunctions there were offered at the summit.
t.Feroz: The Children of Wrecks attacked the battered town of Oran seeking Governor Rahab's imagined treasure, but the raid was turned back with the help of the Mora's Rock garrison.
t.Holberg: A conjunction was offered to kill all the greenteeth at Sacrifice Point in Misericorde.
t.Kallavesa: It was a tumultuous season: yegarra crossed the Westmere to strike Hufi's Garden, and bandits threatened Salagiin traders on the Gullet, as a strange toad creature warned. Conjunctions there included meeting the ghodi.
t.Liathaven: A Jotun host erupted out of Liathaven to invade Bregasland.
t.Mareave: With the Ayereed beachhead gone, the Salt Lords once again control Mareave's southern borders.
t.Mitwold: Yegarra threatened John's Holt in Meade March, and the Drakes and other Imperial armies may billet here.
t.Morrow: The Archmage of Winter was responsible for performing the Ward of the Black Waste in Altis. Border patrols raise the Druj beachhead threshold.
t.Mournwold: Two armies fought Jotun champions and freed the Ore Hills once again, and a conjunction targeted Einar the Cunning at Alderly.
t.Ossium: Wreckers disguised as merchants landed in Bittershore, butchered travellers on the Iron Roads, and moved to pillage Marshstand Skerry.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Reikos readied themselves for the coming year.
t.Reinos: Five Imperial armies invaded, conquering Ribeira and almost all of Bastasor, while the Lasambrian Jotun fought on. A battle opportunity and conjunctions there were offered.
t.Sarangrave: Four armies from Lustri defeated Druj armies and the Tower of the Skink garrison in the Bloodwater Marsh, but had yet to claim a beachhead.
t.Sarvos: Officer cadets were offered the chance to interrogate a Grendel captain at Uccelini, and the traitor Maurizia Spada was said to plan raids on Sarvos.
t.Segura: Five armies marched out of Segura into Reinos, and conjunctions in Burnish invited Imperials to draw and name constellations.
t.Sermersuaq: A body awaited investigation in Stark, and cultists of the Claw headed back into Sermersuaq through Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Skarsind: Cultists of the Claw stole almost a dozen wains of white granite from a Brilliant Shore caravan and fled towards Pakaanan's Pass. If they are not stopped, the Brilliant Shore will yield only 17 wains at Summer.
t.Spiral: A small conjunction was offered to meet followers of Berechiah in Apulus.
t.Tassato: Imperial armies prepared here, while wreckers headed for the Circle of Decay regio in Madeiras to curse Tassato with Thunderous Deluge.
t.The Barrens: Conjunctions offered the chance to exorcise tortured souls at Hope's Rest and to attend the tournament of the Earl of the Groves. Border patrols mean the Druj need 25 victory points for a beachhead.
t.Therunin: With the Imperial armies withdrawn, the Druj conquered the Tarn Valley, assaulted Peakedge Song and woke the vallorn of Tharunind. Several conjunctions were offered here.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Upwold prepared for the year ahead, and armies may billet here.
t.Zenith: Wreckers under Tuomas of Pirenea fled through western Zenith with ilium looted from the Alliance of the Sky, and the Warmage was called to stop them.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Jotun host poured through their magical fortifications at Gravenmarch to invade the fens.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A conjunction was offered to kill all the greenteeth at Drowner's Dell, the responsibility of the Keeper of the Breadbasket.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The battle opportunity to block the Jotun path at Sal-Ott Meet was offered here.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The General of the Strong Reeds was responsible for recovering plundered goods at Sallow's Shallows.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Red-Eyed Reaper was responsible for killing all the greenteeth at Sacrifice Point.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: After yegarra struck Hufi's Garden, the Woundbinder of the Mark was called to defeat them at Hufi's Glen.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Imperial Consul was invited to meet the ghodi at Gull Isle.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Strategos Aeolwulf was asked to intercept, at Whittling Grove, bandits who had trapped Salagiin ships to slaughter their merchants for ilium.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: The Bailiff of Meade was responsible for defeating yegarra at John's Holt.
r.Morrow/Altis: The Archmage of Winter was responsible for performing the Ward of the Black Waste in the Canticulous Valley.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Stanley of Chalkdown was responsible for killing Einar the Cunning at Boar's Hall.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Two Imperial armies freed the Ore Hills from the Jotun once again.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Wreckers posing as Varushkan merchants docked in southern Bittershore before attacking travellers on the Iron Roads.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Cabalist Vasili Zoryakovich Zverokaz was called to ambush the wreckers at Makgore's Grove before they reach Marshstand Skerry.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: Imperial armies conquered almost all of Bastasor, and a battle opportunity to seize the township at Grismont Road was offered.
r.Reinos/Pedreira: The Champion of Prosperity was responsible for recovering Bulangiin Karadghra at Getshold.
r.Reinos/Ribeira: The Empire quickly conquered Ribeira's olive groves and fig orchards, and a conjunction targeted Carmo Stoneblade at Carmo's Sheepfold.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: A battle opportunity against the Druj to influence the vallorn at Mirereach was offered.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Imperial armies won a slow victory against the Druj in the bloodthirsty, teeming marsh.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Cadets were offered the chance to interrogate a Grendel captain at Smugglers Copse.
r.Segura/Burnish: Two conjunctions at the Meadow of Dust and Glass invited Imperials to draw and name constellations and to create lore for them.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind was responsible for investigating a body at Njord Beach Hut.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Cultists of the Claw were fleeing through the pass with stolen granite, and a conjunction at the Cave of Bones offered a bargain with Tuki of the Little Bones.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Voice of Vigilance was responsible for meeting followers of Berechiah at The Cellar Below.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: Wreckers led by Maurizia Spada were heading to the Circle of Decay regio to curse Tassato, and Tongs Barossa was to stop them at Lucrezia's Orchard.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The High Exorcist was responsible for exorcising tortured souls at the Field of Triumph.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Enchanter Morien de Carsenere was responsible for attending the tournament of the Earl of the Groves at Tournament Square.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Blaze Dunning was responsible for destroying a miasma pillar at the Tainted Meadow.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Druj poured in, but defenders and the Tarnfather's blessings preserved the houses of healing. The Eastern Broker was responsible for rescuing an Axou warrior at Catrin's Glade.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The Champion of Vigilance was responsible for killing the Lord of Thorns at Broken Copse.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Tuomas of Pirenea's wreckers sailed up the Couros into Iteri to loot ilium, and the Warmage was called to retrieve it at Lutum Woods.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Four Imperial armies marched through Lustri's night-haunted forests to attack the Sarangrave.

A box for a sword.d: The Waning Circle bought out the Street of Grains and will buy weirwood, mithril and white granite through Ephisis' Scale, with prices dropping as more wains are offered. Ilium prices are withheld until after the ilium seat auction. At Vossk's request, the Sovereign-Lord of the City of Chains offered the Argent Sword, a raiding army costing 300 mithril and 900 crowns with 50 thrones upkeep. It can only be raised if Callidus has amity, a Senate motion authorises it and it is placed under the Military Council. The city would pay its upkeep if the Canterspire Circle were ceded to it. Immaculate Architect costs 77 rings of ilium. The Silent Market offers Vermillion Heart spice for cow bonds.

n.Highguard: Arlais of Highguard asked about having the Autumn realm build fortifications in Highguard, which Crown could not make profitable. Instead Crown offered the Immaculate Architect ritual text to the first citizen to send 77 rings of ilium.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are named as having taken possession of the Immaculate Architect ritual text and refusing to return it to the Empire.
n.Urizen: Vossk of the Concordium of Pallas obtained an offer for an Autumn mercenary army to fight under an Urizen banner. It would need Callidus to have amity, Senate authorisation and a general chosen through constitutional means under the Military Council. Her request to buy an Ephisis box was refused.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the description of raiding armies notes that some Wintermark armies find fighting alongside foraging armies distasteful, given their dislike of "maggots".

t.Redoubt: The proposed Argent Sword mercenary army would be raised at Wilstone in Redoubt if the opportunity is commissioned before the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.

A bridge too far.d: The Kongegőr was damaged by an Imperial raid in 384YE, but the Jotun have since rebuilt and heavily fortified it, so a repeat raid by fleets and military units cannot succeed. One option is for an army to take full control of Alsterbo or Bjarkey and then destroy the bridges in a season. The alternative depends on the Marcher and Wintermark assemblies each enacting a mandate urging fleets to support the Red Wind Corsairs. The Corsairs would then take to the sea from Mitwold, Kallavesa or Bregasland, backed by at least 5,000 points of fleets. After that they could launch a shore offensive on Alsterbo. Graciana warned that a Jotun counter-attack was likely.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Graciana considered and rejected enlisting the Grendel, expecting them to betray the plan to the Jotun, and she recalled her earlier appraisal on disrupting Grendel activity in the Bay of Catazar.
n.Jotun: Destroying the Kongegőr's bridges would stop Jotun armies moving between Narkyst and Kalsea. The Jotun have heavily fortified the causeway against fleets and raids, though they would not expect an attack by a navy.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly would need to enact a mandate urging its fleets to support the Red Wind Corsairs. Mitwold is one of the possible launch points, though the Marches have nowhere near enough fleets on their own.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark assembly would also need to enact the mandate, and Wintermark has at least twice the required fleet strength. Its lands offer Kallavesa as a launch point and Sermersuaq as a route into Skallahn.

t.Bay of Catazar: Warships built on the Bay to let the Red Wind Corsairs put to sea were due for completion by the coming summit. Without local fleet support, the Corsairs could only sail in these waters.
t.Bregasland: Now in Jotun hands, Bregasland is one of the territories the Empire would have to fight through to reach Hordalant. It is also named as one of the places the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea from.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant anchors the southern end of the Kongegőr and is heavily fortified. The Empire's information about it rests on a spy network several years old.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa is one of the three territories where the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea, with Wintermark fleet support, to begin an assault on the Kongegőr.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named as a Jotun-held territory the Empire would need to pass through to reach Hordalant overland.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is one of the three territories where the Red Wind Corsairs could take to the sea with Marcher and Wintermark fleet support.
t.Sermersuaq: As firmly Imperial territory bordering Skallahn, Sermersuaq is the starting point for any overland push on Greenwall and then Bjarkey.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn anchors the northern end of the Kongegőr. It looks the easier overland target, but it is defended by the walls of Kierheim and a smaller fortification at Ulfsmoor.

r.Hordalant/Alsterbo: Alsterbo anchors the southern end of the Kongegőr and is protected by a small fortification at Dalvi. It is the target of the proposed naval shore offensive, which would have to capture the region before the bridges could be destroyed.
r.Hordalant/Ashahon: The Fortress of the Pale Queen in Ashahon, a rank two fortification of cultural significance to the Jotun, would make any Imperial capture of Alsterbo harder.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: Bjarkey anchors the northern end of the Kongegőr and is guarded by the level two walls of Kierheim, seat of the Jarl of Kierheim. An army in full control of the region could destroy the bridges.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Imperial armies would have to seize Greenwall first, possibly within a single season, before they could reach Bjarkey.

A circle sewn with fate.d: After being rebuffed at Redoubt, the Children of Wrecks sent their Gathered Storm navy, led by the flagship Storm's Child and backed by carcharodons and a guardian of Siakha, south from Madruga to sack Oran. At the same time Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse led almost the entire garrison of Mora's Rock towards the town. Both forces arrived together. The Grendel broke the western gate, ignored the Freeborn and slaughtered the pirates, aided by Grendel sleeper agents and the corsairs. After three hours the Children fled into the Cazar Straits. Saoirse explained the intelligence that made this possible had come from a 'ghost of the sea' and a now-burned spy ring. She urged the Freeborn to prepare their own defences or seek an accord with Mora's Rock. Fiersach and Saoirse will accept winged messengers.

n.Grendel: The Mora's Rock garrison under Commander Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse defeated the Children of Wrecks at Oran out of contempt for them as traitors, then returned to Morajasse. They lost the use of part of their espionage ring and now invite Imperial messengers.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications in Necropolis are among the few coastal defences, and the Highborn traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is confirmed dead.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the closest Imperial forces to Oran had already crossed into Reinos, too far away to help.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn of Oran were saved from a Children of Wrecks sack by the Grendel and their own corsairs. They were warned to prepare their defences or persuade their leaders to reach an accord with Mora's Rock.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: fortifications in Sarvos and Spiral are named among the few protections against surprise attack from the sea.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the recap recalls the Grendel and Children of Wrecks attacks on Elos and Visten, and the Gyre coven's magical storms over Redoubt.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: anxiety gripped the whole bay as the Grendel armada and the Children of Wrecks' fleets remained at large.
t.Feroz: Oran was attacked by the Children of Wrecks and saved by the Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock. The Empire still controls three regions, while the Children and the Grendel hold one apiece.
t.Madruga: The Gathered Storm sailed south from Madruga to attack Oran. The territory remains uncontrolled, with three regions held by the Empire, one by the Children of Wrecks and three uncontrolled.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: named as the eastern edge of the Bay of Catazar, where the air was thick with anticipation.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications are one of the few defences against a surprise attack from the sea.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the recap notes the failed Grendel and Children of Wrecks attacks on Elos and the Gyre coven's storms that struck Redoubt.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial forces were already across the border into Reinos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications help guard the southern coast against sea raids.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Oran's garrison sent desperate messages west to Segura for help.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: its fortifications help guard the southern coast against sea raids.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: Some citizens of Oran fled south-east on foot across the grasslands towards Afarjasse to escape the coming battle.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Corsair refugees from the Cazar Straits fought hard against the Children at Oran, and the beaten Gathered Storm retreated into the Straits' waters.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: fleeing citizens chose not to go south into Fontargenta, fearing the Children of Wrecks would follow them.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Grendel garrison of Mora's Rock marched out of Morajasse to fight at Oran, then returned there with their dead and injured.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Children of Wrecks tried to conquer Oranseri and pillage Oran, but the Grendel and local corsairs drove them off after three hours of fighting in the town.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Mentioned in passing: a band of youths set out through the Siroc Bayou to seek help from Quzar.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: the traitor Ezhabbenar of Hedrossan is confirmed dead after the Winter Solstice battle.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Mentioned in passing: the recap recalls the Children of Wrecks' attempt to devastate the spires of Visten.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: refugees dared not take the road to Lucksprings with a Grendel force crossing the grasslands.

A peerless sacrifice.d: Peerless kinship had let Highguard aid the Freeborn in Kahraman, the Dawnish in the Barrens, the orcs of Skarsind and the Marches in the Mournwold, with Therunin to follow. After a Greater Majority statement by Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard, the faithful proved unable to sustain both kinship and crusade, so competing mandates were offered. The Assembly upheld Judgement 116, sending Brother Olyvar of Esther's Sanctum to urge embracing peerless kinship. The Assembly may now choose any nation to aid, though not the same nation two seasons running. Highborn armies will no longer automatically generate mandates. The Benefactors' Council, which could have redirected Highguard's ten wains each season to any civilian commission, kept them going to the Grand Inspiration of the Way.

n.Dawn: Dawn had earlier received Highborn peerless kinship to help contact the factions in the Barrens, and its people could be chosen again under the retained power.
n.Highguard: Highguard chose peerless kinship over crusade, so its armies no longer automatically generate mandates. Its benefactors kept donating ten wains a season of white granite towards the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs had been helped through peerless kinship to better understand the Ossium septs, and remain eligible for future Highborn aid.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a renewed crusade power would likely have taken the form of the recent call for an ongoing crusade against the Jotun, but this option was not chosen.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were named as the next recipients of Highborn peerless kinship in Therunin, and the Highborn were preparing for war with the vallorn alongside the returning grey pilgrims.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn had received Highborn peerless kinship in Kahraman, and the retained power means the Brass Coast could be aided again in future.
n.The Marches: The Marches had been helped by Highguard to deal with threats in the Mournwold, and Highborn armies rested and resupplied in Upwold this season.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not discussed, though Highborn benefactors from a group called Reumah's Redoubt are listed.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Highborn kinship helped the Imperial Orcs understand the septs of Ossium, a Varushkan territory.

t.Astolat: Highborn armies took a much-needed rest in Astolat this season, resupplying rather than campaigning.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was one of the places where Highguard's peerless kinship had helped the Freeborn.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: an in-character vignette notes that a listed benefactor is a corsair from Madruga.
t.Mournwold: Highguard's peerless kinship had helped the Marches deal with threats in the Mournwold.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Highborn kinship had helped the Imperial Orcs better understand the Ossium septs.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed, though benefactors of Reumah's Redoubt appear in the list.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was where Highborn kinship had helped the Imperial Orcs better understand the Ossium septs.
t.The Barrens: Highguard's peerless kinship had aided the Dawnish in contacting the factions of the Barrens.
t.Therunin: Therunin was named as the next place where Highguard would offer peerless kinship in the weeks to come.
t.Upwold: Highborn armies rested and resupplied in Upwold this season instead of campaigning.

A pillow of winds.d: Faraden asked what non-military help it could give against the Jotun, and suggested capturing Flareizo, Chaveiro and Cimeira. High Lord Ganzorig Muhnkhabat asked for a Rod and Shield honour guard to escort his war-wizards to Anvil through Reinos, while Mistress Karadragha proposed that the Celestial Arch soften the visit's political impact. Caitun now offered luxury goods in place of weltsilver. The Hakhandra family offered to buy Marcher cattle bonds, and the Tseriyn offered mithril for gloaming. The Parador of Wind and Flame was completed at the Azure Chorus. A Holberg trading enclave awaited the Chamber of Commerce's choice of goods. Conservative Faraden priests invited Imperial preachers, and the Ember Blossoms sought Freeborn passage to Asavea.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: described as the opportunistic Asavean ally already in the Empire's back yard.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the nations a Faraden caravan could trade with along the Blood Red Roads.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden ambassador said any Sand Fishers visiting Holberg would be welcomed as Imperial Orcs are.
n.Jotun: The Faraden treaty with the Jotun stopped Faraden aiding the Imperial invasion of Reinos. The civil service warned that this peace holds only while the Jotun focus on the Empire, and the proposed Muhnkhabat journey through Reinos risked provoking them.
n.The Brass Coast: The Azure Sutannir completed the Parador of Wind and Flame in Kahraman and gained added weight with the Faraden. Separately, the Ember Blossoms sought the Freeborn National Assembly's help in reaching Asavea.
n.The League: Faraden remained keen on a trading enclave in Holberg but needed the Holberg Chamber of Commerce to choose cloth, spice, iron or none. The ambassador also answered League concerns about orcs, the Holberg Gate and the Bishops' judgement.
n.The Marches: The Hakhandra offered to buy up to 16 Marcher cattle bonds and would back Yakholme Grange, and the Tseriyn offered the Alder of Meade mithril for iridescent gloaming. Faraden appetite for Marcher food and Upwold confectionery remained strong.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: listed as a nation a Faraden caravan could trade with on its way across the Empire.

t.Holberg: Faraden proposed the Firewind Market and a caravan enclave with a Hall of Five Flames in Holberg, pending the Chamber of Commerce's choice of trade goods. Faraden merchants might avoid the Holberg Gate because of its False Flame aura.
t.Kahraman: The Parador of Wind and Flame was completed at the Azure Chorus, drawing Faraden entertainers to celebrate alongside Imperial pilgrims, though their journey still meant paying Jotun tolls in Reinos.
t.Mitwold: Faraden merchants were waiting to see whether Mitwold or Upwold became the leading cattle market before choosing where to trade, and the Hakhandra sought cattle bonds from both markets.
t.Reinos: The Court of Five Winds welcomed the Imperial invasion but could not send troops. It sought other ways to help drive out the Jotun, and the Muhnkhabat planned a provocative journey through the Lasambrian Hills.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Faraden ambassador called the sea of snow too dangerous for safe commerce, which is why Faraden merchants will not take to ships.
t.Upwold: The Marcher ambassador proposed reviving Moonwater Hall in Upwold as Yakholme Grange, and Upwold's liquorice confectionery was in fashion among wealthy Faraden. Faraden merchants were still weighing Upwold against Mitwold as a cattle market.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, which is linked here through the wider Holberg enclave plans, including a Firewind Market in the upper city.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The parkland of Holmauer was favoured for the Faraden caravan enclave, and a small Hall of Five Flames temple there was described as a deal-breaker for the merchant families.
r.Reinos/Chaveiro: Faraden named the capture of Chaveiro as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.
r.Reinos/Cimeira: Faraden named the capture of Cimeira as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.
r.Reinos/Flareizo: Faraden named the capture of Flareizo as one of three conquests that would best secure a safe land trade route between the two nations.

A pinch of salt.d: After Aliss Thorn's mandate sent artisans to Oakwood, the recovered smiths revealed their lost art was forging bargains, not crafting. A friar proposed the Stone Smith's Workshop sinecure, costing 8 white granite, 8 mithril, 8 ilium and 6 thrones, built at the Woldstone (Ashbrook, Upwold) or the Maiden Stone (Maiden Downs, Mitwold). The Stone Smith, appointed by the Tally of the Votes, would receive 1 throne each season; if a smith, they would also gain a pauper's key each Spring and, through Renna Whitesmith's ancient bargain with the herald Gull, an annual plenipotentiary-like invitation to an eternal each Autumn. Upwold and Mitwold smiths dispute the site. The opportunity ends if not commissioned by the Winter Solstice 387YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches may revive the smiths' lost art of bargaining by commissioning a workshop and electing a Stone Smith, though rival Upwold and Mitwold smiths have left the choice of site to the nation.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold is one of two candidate locations for the Stone Smith's Workshop, and its returned smiths insist the Maiden Stone should be chosen.
t.Upwold: Upwold is one of two candidate locations for the Stone Smith's Workshop, with its smiths, including Jack Hammersmith, arguing for the Woldstone.

r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: The Maiden Stone on the Maiden Downs, a site echoing with magic, is proposed as a possible home for the Stone Smith's Workshop.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The Woldstone at Ashbrook, the regio where the smiths were trapped for centuries, is proposed as a possible home for the Stone Smith's Workshop.

Construct Beneficiary of the Golden Casc.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Zenith's, the motion built a sinecure arising from the Forwards and Rewards wind of fortune, at a cost of 8 weirwood, 8 white granite and 6 thrones, taking three months to complete. Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged provided the thrones and materials after the Spring Equinox. The title, appointed by the Urizen Assembly, requires its holder to use the proceeds to aid and reward other nations to build international friendship and cooperation. Each season the holder receives 20 random herbs, 3 elixir vitae, 3 ossean solutions, 3 philtres of heavenly lore and 10 crowns, while the Virtue Fund gains an additional 10 crowns.

n.Urizen: Urizen gained a new title whose holder, appointed by the Urizen Assembly, is charged with using its herbs, potions and crowns to aid and reward other nations and foster international friendship.

t.Zenith: The sinecure was built in Zenith, with Zenith's senator seconding the motion, and was complete in time for its first appointment at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris became home to the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, built with weirwood and white granite supplied by Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged.

Construct Chamber of Euphony.d: Proposed by the senator for Spiral and seconded by Tassato, the motion followed the opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune 'The play that came to Apulian'. It cost 15 mithril, 12 ilium and 5 thrones and took three months to build. Funding came from private donors across 387YE, including Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below, Rafael, Genoveva and Dagon Barossa, Rhys Nighthaven, Gideon of the suns of Couros and Farren Silver Streams. The Map to the City Below is appointed annually by the League National Assembly. It is revocable by the League or General Assemblies or the Assembly of Nine, and oversees the fane while encouraging magic, music and mystery in Apulian. With the work complete, the title became available to appoint for the first time.

n.The League: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Map to the City Below, which its National Assembly appoints each year. Much of the funding came from League citizens such as members of the Barossa family and Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below.

t.Spiral: Spiral's senator proposed the motion, and the territory gained the Chamber of Euphony, a fane dedicated to Sung.

r.Spiral/Apulus: The Chamber of Euphony was built in Apulus, and its titleholder is charged with spreading magic, music and mystery in the city of Apulian.

Construct Hylje Dolmen.d: Logan Dunning, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced a self-funded commission for a white granite marker dolmen on the northern shores of the Rikkivessi. It was meant to let the Hylje bring up from the depths the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell during the invasion of Sermersuaq while helping to protect Wintermark citizens. The Imperial Orcs would then collect the remains for proper funerary care. The project cost 10 white granite and 30 crowns and took three months. Raal Dunn provided the money and the granite after the Spring Equinox. On completion it created the Custodian of Bones, a position with tenure that the senators of Wintermark can appoint.
