n.Imperial Orcs: The dolmen was built so that the bones of Imperial Orc heroes who fell defending Sermersuaq could be recovered from the depths by the Hylje and collected by the Imperial Orcs for proper funerary care.
n.Wintermark: The completed dolmen honours the orcs who died protecting Wintermark citizens, and Wintermark's senators gained the right to appoint the new Custodian of Bones, a position with tenure.

t.Sermersuaq: A new sinecure, a white granite dolmen on the northern shores of the Rikkivessi, was built in Sermersuaq to recover the remains of orc heroes who fell during the territory's invasion.

r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq became the site of the white granite marker dolmen where the Hylje deliver recovered orc bones, and it is the seat of the new Custodian of Bones.

Construct Lumi's Legacy.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the commission created a herb sinecure called Lumi's Legacy in East Floes, Sermersuaq, intended to focus on bladeroot cultivation. It required 10 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns and three months to complete. Lumi Warmthbringer funded it in full, providing 3 thrones 6 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox. The title of Legal Leaseholder of Lumi's Legacy carries tenure and is chosen by the unanimous decision of the Wintermark senators. With the work complete, the first appointment was due at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the construction was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new herb sinecure in its own lands, funded by Lumi Warmthbringer. Its senators hold the power to appoint the tenured Leaseholder by unanimous decision.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq became home to Lumi's Legacy, a new bladeroot-growing sinecure built in the territory.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: it appears only in the name of the Master of Rings, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, who announced the construction.

r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: East Floes is the site of Lumi's Legacy, a herb sinecure focused on bladeroot cultivation. It was completed and ready for its first Leaseholder at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

Construct Meeting Place.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion committed the Empire to 55 wains of white granite and 198 crowns of labour, with the Jotun contributing to the joint build. The full edifice cost 110 wains of white granite and 396 crowns, raised because it was built in a marsh, and took nine months. Andos, speaking for the Jarl of Kierheim, supplied 24 thrones, 6 crowns and 55 wains of granite. Fedelmidd Sydanjaa's Heart Floer supplied 24 thrones, 1 crown and 55 wains. Further small sums came from three others. The motion followed the wind of fortune "A stone for a stone".

n.Jotun: The Jotun were partners in the build, with Andos speaking for the Jarl of Kierheim providing half the granite and a large share of the money, giving them a dedicated diplomatic hall with the Empire.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark territory gained Gull's Isle Hall as a meeting place with the Jotun, after a motion proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq.

t.Kallavesa: Gull's Isle Hall now stands on Gull Island in Kallavesa as a feasting hall and meeting place for diplomacy between the Empire and the Jotun.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The hall was built on Gull Island in the West Marsh, and building in the marsh raised the labour costs.

Construct Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hos.d: Announced by Arlen Foreman-Smith, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, the hospital creates the Warden of the Weary, who provides shelter and succour to travellers in Astolat and is paid 18 drams of cerulean mazzarine each season from the hospital gardens. The announcement named 10 wains of weirwood from the Castellan of Spiral Castle. Construction required standard costs, 10 weirwood and 30 crowns over three months. Tallis Hart provided 3 thrones, 4 crowns and the 10 wains of weirwood after the Spring Equinox, and Farren Silver Streams and Rhyn Huckster gave a crown each. Once complete, the Warden was to be appointed by tally of the votes of Dawn's military unit captains, first at the Summer Solstice 387YE for a reduced one-season term.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a new hospital in its territory of Astolat, and the military unit captains of Dawn choose its Warden of the Weary by tally of their votes.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the announcement named the Castellan of Spiral Castle, in a League territory, as the source of the weirwood for construction.

t.Astolat: A memorial hospital is built in Astolat, whose Warden of the Weary will offer shelter and succour to travellers across the territory.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the announcement named the Castellan of Spiral Castle as supplying the 10 wains of weirwood for the hospital.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: Winterbourne is the site of the new Rhydian Sepulchre Memorial Hospital, whose gardens yield 18 drams of cerulean mazzarine each season to pay its Warden.

Construct Statue of that Cockscroft Lad.d: Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Mistress of Monuments, announced the statue in Spring 387YE to celebrate the Vigilant hue and cry raised by Johnathan Piper of the Cockscroft and to mark the site where the Wayford Wanderers and their supporters were massacred in Mitwold. The announcement stated it was funded by the Cockscroft Household, at a cost of 5 white granite and 15 crowns plus standard costs, taking three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Bolotnikov provided 1 throne 7 crowns and 5 wains of white granite. The completed statue of Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft now stands in pride of place near the site of the senseless loss of life.

n.The Marches: A Marcher household, the Cockscroft, funded a monument honouring one of its own, Johnathan Piper, for his Vigilant hue and cry, and the statue now commemorates the Wayford Wanderers massacre on Marcher soil.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold gained a completed statue marking the site of the massacre of the Wayford Wanderers and their supporters.

r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: The statue of Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft was built in Maiden Downs and now stands in pride of place near the site of the massacre.

Construct Stone Smith's Workshop.d: The workshop was meant as a place where smiths could gather, talk, keep a repository of lore and train new smiths. It also created the Stone Smith position, to be appointed by tally of the votes, and the sinecure was to be self-funded. Construction followed the terms of the related opportunity and needed 8 white granite, 8 mithril, 8 ilium and 6 thrones over three months. After the Spring Equinox 387YE Gemma Brightsmith supplied the ilium and white granite and Orrick the thrones. After the Summer Solstice Orrick, Watkin, Annie Webster and Willum of Goatsbridge supplied the mithril. With the workshop complete, the Stone Smith was to be elected for the first time by tally of the votes of Marcher farm owners at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators proposed and seconded the motion, and Marchers supplied the materials. The new Stone Smith title is chosen by a tally of votes cast by Marcher farm owners.

t.Upwold: The workshop was built in Upwold, giving the territory a centre for smithing lore and training. Upwold's senator seconded the motion.

r.Upwold/Ashbrook: The Stone Smith's Workshop stands in the Woldstone in Ashbrook, where smiths can gather, keep their lore and train apprentices.

Construct Tower of the Dragon.d: The tower was commissioned as an opportunity arising from the Stone and Stone Wind of Fortune. Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, announced it as fully funded by herself and the Archmage of Summer, Mirella of the Twisted Rose, at a cost of 15 white granite and 45 crowns, taking three months to complete. After the Spring Equinox Dima provided 3 thrones and 15 wains of white granite, Mirella and Kostjya each gave a throne, and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost added 5 crowns. On completion the Archmage of Summer gained a ministry allowing them to trade tempest jade for Jewels from the Deep Mountain.

n.Varushka: A new ministry for the Archmage of Summer was raised in Varushkan-held Ossium, funded largely by the Master of the Koboldi, with further contributions from Kostjya and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost.

t.Ossium: Ossium became home to the Tower of the Dragon, the Archmage of Summer's official residence and a ministry trading tempest jade for Jewels from the Deep Mountain.

r.Ossium/Nearweald: The Tower of the Dragon was built in Nearweald using white granite and crowns, completed as the Archmage of Summer's residence and ministry.

Construct Wanderer's Entertainment Socie.d: Announced by Lucrezia Corvinascura, Chair of the Wolf, and organised by Red Ravens Holding, the project required 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns (3 thrones and 6 crowns) at standard costs, taking three months to complete. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the full materials and money after the Spring Equinox 387YE. Once complete, the Mistress of Festivities, a sinecure providing wealth, became available for the League Assembly to appoint by judgement for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE. At the Autumn Equinox 387YE the Senate granted the powers and responsibilities of the Mistress of Festivities to the Mistress of Ceremonies.

n.The League: The League gained a new wealth-producing sinecure, the Mistress of Festivities, appointed by the League Assembly, though its powers were later folded into the Mistress of Ceremonies by the Senate.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar became home to the Wanderer's Entertainment Society, a new Imperial structure funded by Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Wanderer's Entertainment Society was built in Hanuri, completed after three months of construction.

Construct Wayhouse in Ossium.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Mitwold, the motion commissioned a wayhouse in the Varushkan territory of Ossium, in the region of Nearweald, linked to the Way Home Wind of Fortune. It cost 16 wains of mithril and 6 thrones and was to take three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox, Gryiff Embercast provided the 16 wains of mithril and 5 thrones 7 crowns, and Farren Silver Streams provided 1 crown. Once complete, the Strategos of Navarr gains custodianship of a sinecure, and Navarr can take personal resources in Ossium without the usual foreign nation penalty.

n.Navarr: Navarr gains a wayhouse in Ossium that shelters its refugees from Therunin, gives the Strategos of Navarr custodianship of a sinecure to help fund the army, and lets Navarri take personal resources in Ossium without the foreign nation penalty.
n.Varushka: Varushka's territory of Ossium will host a Navarr wayhouse and Navarri settlers drawing resources there without penalty.

t.Ossium: A Navarr wayhouse is commissioned in Ossium, allowing Navarri to hold personal resources in this Varushkan territory without the foreign nation penalty.
t.Therunin: Navarri refugees displaced from Therunin are to be housed at the new wayhouse in Ossium.

r.Ossium/Nearweald: Nearweald is the site of the new Navarr wayhouse, which is to take three months to build and will house refugees from Therunin.

Construct Wharfage of Oran.d: Proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by Kahraman, the motion commissioned the Wharfage of Oran, following the Send for me Wind of Fortune. It cost 15 weirwood and 15 crowns, was fully self-funded and took three months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Esteban I Del Rio Blanco I Guerra provided 1 throne, 6 crowns and 15 wains of weirwood, and Farren Silver Streams gave 1 crown. Once complete, the lawless quality was removed from the Cazar Straits. The new Corsair of Oran receives 216 rings and, if held by a corsair, a yearly base fleet upgrade. It was first appointable by the votes of Freeborn fleet owners at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named in the motion and is linked only as one of the powers holding part of Feroz that season.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new sinecure in Feroz, with Freeborn fleet owners choosing the first Corsair of Oran at the Summer Solstice 387YE, and the motion was proposed by Feroz and seconded by Kahraman.

t.Feroz: The Wharfage of Oran was built in Feroz, and its construction ended the lawless state of the territory's Cazar Straits.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: With the wharfage complete, the Cazar Straits lost their lawless quality.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Wharfage of Oran was constructed at Oran in Oranseri, the seat of the new Corsair of Oran title.

Damming the Doubt.d: The proposed dam would flood the Fallen Valley, where soldiers who died at the Battle of Solen's Doubt lie buried, and send much of the Doubt's water to Icarion. The site is haunted and exposed to the Black Plateau. Nisha Strascovich enacted a Varushkan mandate sending volhovs to ward the dam against ghosts. Illarawm mystagogues began recovering Imperial Orc bones, protected by League priests preaching Loyalty. Carving the names of the fallen into the dam would add 5 thrones to its cost. Halkyon of the Myriad Stream made a statement in the Urizen assembly, and amity was granted to Ylenwe. The Senate, or a suitable title holder, has yet to commission the dam.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named in the account of the final battle at Solen's Doubt, in which thousands of Imperial soldiers died.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly asked that bonetenders reclaim the remains of orcs who fell at Solen's Doubt and that their names be carved into the dam's stones. Illarawm mystagogues are now travelling to Apstrus to recover the bones, despite the grave danger the Black Plateau poses to orc priests.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly had not yet spoken on the matter. Freeborn custom treats life as a matter for the living, and many of their fallen were likely cremated.
n.The League: Rafael Barossa d'Apulian's statement embraced flooding the battle site, in keeping with Leaguish funeral customs. Fabio Costas d'Apulian, Sofonisba Amilcara of the City Below and Merlof Von Temeschwar led their congregations to Apstrus to protect the mystagogues.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly was invited to decide how its dead at Solen's Doubt should be treated and whether the spire's library should be preserved. Halkyon of the Myriad Stream made a well-regarded statement that passed with a greater majority, and its outcome is still to come.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly backed the reservoir, asked that the deeds of the dead be recognised, and enacted a mandate through Nisha Strascovich. Volhovs will travel to Spiral to ward the dam and its workers against restless spirits.

t.Mareave: The dam is part of ongoing efforts to relieve the aridity of Mareave by redirecting much of the River Doubt into the territory.
t.Spiral: Spiral would gain a dam and a large reservoir, built on haunted ground under threat from the Black Plateau. With amity now granted, the eternal Ylenwe is able to aid the work, and zie has offered plans for a protective fane if friendship lasts a year.

r.Mareave/Icarion: A good portion of the River Doubt's waters would be redirected to Icarion to ease its aridity.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The dam and reservoir would flood the Fallen Valley beside the abandoned spire of Solen's Doubt. Volhovs are coming to ward the site against ghosts, mystagogues are recovering orc bones there, and the River Doubt below would be much reduced.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the madness lying in wait at the heart of Screed threatens any army working on the dam.

Doing it.d: Barien's heralds confirmed that everyone receiving Challenge the Iron Duke would be guaranteed entry to one challenge per summit, choosing a reward from the Dragonforge. Past victors must wait a year to compete again. Six covens had cast the magnitude 30 ritual the previous season. In the Challenge of the Caged Pincer, each challenger and two attendants would fight a dire astacid and its two handlers at the Green Iron Grove in Icarion. In the Challenge of the Black Web, challengers would gather glowing tokens in a chamber resembling the Forest of Arden, reached via Alderly. Venomous spider heralds of Jaheris would stalk them there. The in-character text hints at unease over Jaheris's eagerness to help.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish Coven of Golden Wings is listed among the covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: dire astacids are described as giant lobster war beasts common among the Grendel.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named directly; the orcs involved are the now-independent gladiators of Beoraidh on the Broken Shore.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr coven The Eternal Family is listed among the covens that cast Challenge the Iron Duke last season.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: The Glass Mantle and The Tempest Flame, both Brass Coast covens, are listed among those that cast the ritual last season.
n.The Marches: Alderly in the Marcher-held Mournwold was chosen as the point where the Black Web challenge's conjunction would open, because the land there grows close to the Forest of Arden.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark covens Ursolskin and Voices of the Unbound Storm are listed among those that cast the ritual last season.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page; it is linked only through the wider events of the challenges.
t.Mareave: Mareave was the setting for the Challenge of the Caged Pincer, with a large conjunction open for spectators to watch Imperial challengers fight dire astacids.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold provided the conjunction point at Alderly for the Black Web stealth challenge, a short walk from the forest chamber.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Barien's heralds paid the gladiators of independent Beoraidh to supply two dire astacids and handlers for the arena challenge.
r.Mareave/Icarion: The Caged Pincer bouts were set to take place at the Green Iron Grove in Icarion on the Saturday afternoon.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The conjunction for the Challenge of the Black Web was set to open to Alderly, where the land grows close to the Forest of Arden.

Eat like kings.d: After Barthek, Lorekeeper of Meraud, collected the Empire's sacrifices, including a thousand ingots of tempest jade from the League's Golden Chalice, the eternal emerged changed and ambitious to expand his domain. Hayaak's attempt to intercept the sacrifices failed. Golden Ramparts, Lions of Phoenix Reach and Noble Mien of the Hawk Lords work normally, though he asked that the last be renamed. From the Mouths of Babes is suspended, and Golden Trumpets can no longer be cast. He will restore and modify the Churnspire Adjutor regalia and double his golden apples. He named Katrina Words and Leo the Rainbow Sage Golden Lions, each able to codify one ritual. He gave twenty apples to the Archmage of Summer and offered the Golden Chalice a mountain-raising projection.

n.Dawn: Events in Dawn, described in the companion Golden magicians fayre wind, were the first sign that Meraud had recovered, as his heralds came to Dawn as part of his wider enchantment.
n.The League: The League magicians of the Golden Chalice gave a thousand ingots of tempest jade without expecting a boon, and in return Meraud offered their Grandmaster a magnitude 80 arcane projection, The Hands that Shake the Heavens, to raise a mountain. He also proposed himself as the coven's patron, on condition that the projection is used and not codified.
n.Urizen: Meraud confirmed that Lions of Phoenix Reach will keep working as long as the Urizen do not abandon the Three Pillars. The renaming of Noble Mien of the Hawk Lords could earn a more powerful projection that may be placed in Urizen lore.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not discussed; 'Spiral' appears only in former names of the Noble Mien of the Hawk Lords ritual, Lore of the Spiral Dance and Lore of the Golden Spiral.

Fair play is turnabout.d: After the Empire killed Jarl Haakon Gydasson honourably rather than in a way that pleased Basileia, Mistress Alabaster of the Guild of Accountants accepted some of Haakon's belongings as down payment and was given the name of Salt Lord Seonag, de facto chair of the Council of Salt Lords. She demanded forty measures each of Ambergelt, Beggar's lye, Dragonbone and Iridescent gloaming up front, warned it could take years, and promised only an opportunity for Imperial heroes to strike. She warned that reciprocity would expose Anvil's dignitaries to Grendel contracts. Separately, bribery contracts were distributed via Enchanter Edmund Torawyr, one foreign bribe offer was extended to Autumn 387YE, and Overseer Hook and the Union of Lock-Keepers offered further services via Plenipotentiary.

n.Grendel: The Grendel face a potential City of Locks-brokered assassination of Salt Lord Seonag, which could throw their politics into turmoil for months; as regular clients of the City, Salt Lords might also commission killings of Imperial figures in return.
n.Jotun: Jarl Haakon's personal effects were sent to Mistress Alabaster, giving Basileia possible leverage over the Jotun, who refuse to deal with the City of Locks and reportedly drown anyone caught doing so.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon's death in the Marcher territory of the Mournwold is cited as an easy target amid Imperial armies, illustrating the Guild's pricing.

t.Bay of Catazar: A successful killing of Salt Lord Seonag would be the biggest political assassination the Bay of Catazar has seen in decades and could open the way for an all-out attack on Grendel fronts.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Haakon was killed in the Mournwold, surrounded by Imperial land and armies, which made him a cheap and easy target compared with Seonag.

Follow me my friend.d: After Quickening Cold Meat raised Tassato's entombed dead to join the Fist of the Mountains, five armies gathered at Burnish: the Fist, the Bloodcloaks, the Autumn Hammers, the Summer Storm and the Bounders. They made a careful, Day-enhanced steady advance into Reinos. Ribeira fell, and the Autumn Hammers plundered it with Callidus's heralds. Bastasor was four-fifths taken, but Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue held, and casualties were light. Some Fist soldiers grew unusually bloodthirsty. Opportunities followed: killing Carmo Stoneblade, rescuing Faraden traders, joining the Balankas Rush, and a battle at Grismont against Jarl Vafri, with the chance to capture Pastor Ximena.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Feroz appears in a list of lands the Lasambrians say were stolen from them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Corazón and Jotun from northern Reikos are said to have reinforced the Arena of Virtue's defence.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Autumn Hammers and the Summer Storm helped conquer Ribeira. The Hammers plundered rich goods with the aid of Callidus's heralds, and the Summer Storm secured access to the Crown of Bastasor. Irontide Skorr was charged with killing Carmo Stoneblade.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost Ribeira and most of Bastasor, holding only Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue. Jarl Vafri now commands Grismont's defence, while Carmo Stoneblade gathers a fyrd to retake Ribeira.
n.The Brass Coast: The campaign was waged to take a blade from the Freeborn's throat, with armies passing through Kahraman and Segura into Reinos. Some of the plunder recovered had clearly been stolen from Segura or Kahraman.
n.The League: Tassato's wealthy and murdered dead were torn from their tombs and the Vassa to march with the Fist of the Mountains. Many Tassatans were left furious and horrified by the desecration.
n.The Marches: The Bounders set out from Mournwold, scouted the route into Reinos and fought in the steady conquest of Ribeira and Bastasor. Their scouts also found a captive Faraden merchant who could be rescued.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains fought beside Tassatan ghouls, which drew the enemy's contempt, and some of its soldiers grew strangely bloodthirsty amid tales of a black dog in its camp. The Bloodcloaks' healers kept losses low but found no thralls to free.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: named by the Lasambrians as one of the lands they say the Empire stole from them.
t.Kahraman: The Imperial armies marched through Kahraman on their way south to Segura, and some loot seized in Reinos had clearly been taken from Kahraman.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro claim western Kalino as ancestral land, and a captured Faraden merchant was bound for the Iron Confederacy.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: named by the Lasambrians as one of the lands they say the Empire stole from them.
t.Mournwold: The Autumn Hammers, the Summer Storm and the Bounders set out from Mournwold to join the campaign against Reinos.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Corazón and Jotun from northern Reikos reinforced the defenders of the Arena of Virtue.
t.Reinos: Reinos remains in Jotun hands, but the Empire conquered Ribeira and controls most of Bastasor. Further gains are likely after the Spring Equinox before the armies must face the fortified passes to the west.
t.Segura: Segura served as the staging ground for the invasion, with five armies and thousands of independent captains camping at Burnish before crossing west into Reinos.
t.Tassato: Quickening Cold Meat raised the territory's entombed and murdered dead as ghouls, leaving shattered tombs on both sides of the Vassa and an angry populace. No living citizens were harmed.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Mentioned in passing: the armies marched through Braydon's Jasse, past the memorial that was once Fort Braydon.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: the armies from Mournwold passed through Southmoor on their way south.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: The Empire took four-fifths of Bastasor, including access to the Crown of Bastasor, but Grismont Township and the Arena of Virtue held out. A battle opportunity offers the chance to defeat Jarl Vafri and complete the conquest.
r.Reinos/Chaveiro: Mentioned in passing: Chaveiro is likely to fall next if nothing changes after the Spring Equinox.
r.Reinos/Cimeira: Mentioned in passing: refugees fled south to Cimeira, and Pastor Ximena had preached the Virtues as far as Cimeira.
r.Reinos/Pedreira: Mentioned in passing: commanders chose not to press west into Pedreira and its fortification, turning south instead.
r.Reinos/Ribeira: Ribeira was conquered and plundered of its oils, wines, jewellery and icons. Carmo Stoneblade is now gathering a fyrd of Jotun and Lasambrians to retake it.
r.Segura/Burnish: The plains of Burnish hosted a grand camp for five armies and six thousand independent captains before the invasion crossed into Reinos.
r.Tassato/Cascatas: Around Cascatas, the bodies of Jotun orcs and yegarra who died attacking the Sapphire Stair were raised as ghouls to join the Fist of the Mountains.

Germinating a city.d: Relations with the Commonwealth improved thanks to progress on the Diplomatenschloss, busier trade at Leerdam and Volkavaar, and the Empire's respect for Commonwealth authority over Viyerda. The Jarmish embassy at Cargo remained a concern. The Senate had not approved the professors' appraisal auction, so they would leave after Spring Equinox unless it did. Their appraisal for Gisli found Siroc sunk beyond rebuilding and Madruga hampered by uncontrolled regions and the Children of Wrecks. They proposed the Municipal Docks great work at Calvos Sound, an optional Sternenmetal Tower giving the Commonwealth five years of exclusive access, and alternatives such as Sarcophan builders, Quzar or Autumn eternals. The docks were commissioned in Winter 387YE and completed before Autumn Equinox 388YE.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn learned that Siroc could not be rebuilt as their Assembly had urged, but were offered the Municipal Docks at Calvos as its successor. The docks would boost Freeborn fleets, businesses and incomes and create a Quaymaster post chosen by Tally of the Votes.
n.The League: The League Assembly's judgement welcoming Commonwealth guests was gratefully received, but it avoided endorsing the Common Good or calling the war against Jarm virtuous. As a result it drew only modest visitors and opened no new opportunity.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the scholars drew on intelligence from the recent scouting by the Unfettered Mind and the Rod and Shield.
n.Wintermark: Gisli 'the Provider' Baerson of Wintermark received the first Beurteilung, reportedly to fulfil an oath. Gisli used it to commission the study of building a new city in Madruga.

t.Holberg: Holberg's invitation to the Commonwealth during its 250th anniversary brought some interest but only a modest number of visitors, as the Lantir War made the voyage dangerous.
t.Madruga: The scholars judged Madruga hard to develop while three regions were uncontrolled and Free Landing was held by the Children of Wrecks. They proposed growing Calvos into a city through the Municipal Docks, which would raise taxation from the territory by 12 thrones a season.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page; the only Urizen link is the scouting intelligence from the Unfettered Mind and the Rod and Shield.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound was the proposed site of the Municipal Docks, which would fortify the region, act as a shipyard for two navies and could house the Sternenmetal Tower. The docks were eventually commissioned and completed in 388YE.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Mentioned in passing: the Crucible was listed as uncontrolled, an obstacle the scholars thought the Military Council could fix with relative ease.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Children of Wrecks' hold on Free Landing was named as the gravest threat to any building work in Madruga. The docks would also let Freeborn fleets hunt the young kraken growing in its waters.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Mentioned in passing: Lightsea is not named directly and falls only under the general assessment of Madruga.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Grasses were listed as uncontrolled, hindering development of the territory.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The ruins of Siroc sank beneath the water when the Scorrero rose, so the city can never be rebuilt there; the region was also uncontrolled. Only Sarcophan experts, at a premium, might manage building in the drowned ruins.

Golden magicians fayre.d: Dawnish characters, and Navarr whose personal resource lay in the Barrens, could each choose one Summer boon for the Spring Equinox, which came with a sense of fierce pride. Meraud, recovering from his malady, appeared changed and now contests Hayaak's old realm with Jaheris. Heralds of Eleonaris and Cathan Canae clashed while offering boons to the armies in Astolat and to frozen citadels, including a permanent citadel in Hope's Rest. Jaheris offered to retune the Harps of Astolat, Adamant and Meraud proposed a college at the Semmerstones, Rhianos boosted questing, and Barien gave Dawnish artisans a schema. The vigilant warned of rising borderline idolatry, and the conjunction means such national weavings may not happen again.

n.Dawn: Every Dawnish citizen could take a Summer boon with a roleplaying effect of fierce pride, and the nation received several offers to accept or decline: the Harps proposal, the Semmerstones college, the Rimebound citadel, questing rewards and Barien's focus schema.
n.Druj: The heralds of Cathan Canae loathe Druj corruption and are eager to fight the servants of the Buruk Tepel. The Thane's proposed citadel would garrison Hope's Rest against the Druj of the Mallum, and some servants of Rhianos accompanied thorns scouting into the Mallum.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Granite Pillar, encamped in Astolat, was among the seven armies eligible for Eleonaris' boon if enchanted with Knights of Glory. Units supporting it would then gain a boon that includes a Golden Apple.
n.Navarr: Navarr who had moved their personal resource to the Barrens could choose a Summer boon and shared its roleplaying effect, and heralds visited the new Navarr wayhouses, steadings and stridings there.
n.The League: The League's Wolves of War, encamped in Astolat, could benefit from Eleonaris' boon if enchanted with Knights of Glory. Some heralds of Rhianos also accompanied questors as far as Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle in Astolat was eligible for Eleonaris' boon and was tested by the warriors of Cathan Canae. If the Semmerstones college is built, the Summer eternals would be less fixated on competing for patronage of the Icy Crag.

t.Astolat: Seven Imperial armies camped here amid visiting heralds. The Bards of the Crescent offered to retune the Harps of Astolat so they yield silver pears and moonberries instead of extra mana, if the Knight-protector of Winter invites them. The vigilant found no sign of Agramant's cults but warned of growing borderline idolatry.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: people in eastern Astolat fear that vallorn abominations will pour out of Brocéliande once plans to fight the vallorn come to fruition.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: some heralds of Rhianos accompanied Dawnish questors as far afield as the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris' heralds camped at Lacuve within sight of the memorial to the invasion of Ossium.
t.Semmerholm: Rival heralds of Eleonaris and Cathan Canae clashed here, causing damage and disruption but no deaths. Adamant and Meraud's servants proposed building the Circle of the Semmerstones college at the stones in Causse.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: a number of Meraud's heralds visited the de Casillon nobles at Spiral Castle, given their shared history.
t.The Barrens: Heralds visited Dawnish settlements, orc septs and Navarr settlers alike, and Cathan Canae's heralds camped at the White Bear construction site. The Thane of the Rimebound Shore offered empowered and permanent frozen citadels for Hope's Rest.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Thane of the Rimebound Shore prowled the banks of the great lake between the Barrens and Therunin.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was under the Summer weaving, and its people met visiting heralds and saw open fighting between the courtiers of Eleonaris and the warriors of Cathan Canae.

r.Astolat/Coombe: If Jaheris' offer is accepted, creatures of the Forest of Arden would congregate in Coombe and it would gain the wild woods quality, raising the labour cost of most commissions there by half. Locals already fear vallornspawn from neighbouring Brocéliande.
r.Astolat/The Chase: The folk of The Chase, who already suffer occasional miasma and vallornspawn, fear being defenceless if abominations pour out of Brocéliande. They are making what preparations they can without support from the Synod, Senate or Military Council.
r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Mentioned in passing: Black Boughs is named as a place from which Astolat's people fear vallorn monsters will come pouring.
r.Brocéliande/Greenweald: Mentioned in passing: Greenweald is named alongside Black Boughs as a feared source of vallorn abominations.
r.Semmerholm/Causse: The proposed Circle of the Semmerstones would stand at the Semmerstones in Causse as an unbreakable college of Summer magic. It must be commissioned before the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Heralds of Cathan Canae roamed the hills of Estmure, already guarded by the castle of the Adamant Gate, while weighing how best to protect Dawn.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: The heralds of Eleonaris established a camp at Lacuve, around the Dawnish end of the Golden Causeway.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: A frozen citadel raised here every season for a year would give Hope's Rest the Rimebound quality, and 100 rings of ilium could summon the Thane's own citadel as a permanent, upkeep-free fortification against the Druj. That offer stands until the Spring Equinox 388YE.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Heralds of Rhianos made a particular point of seeking out the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Bleaks, to the chagrin of the already unhappy Karass.

High hopes.d: Marcher farm owners drove cattle to market after the Winter Solstice, receiving 484 Stockland and 334 Wayford bonds. Imperial Orcs needed at least 240 bonds to found a Southern Herd in Nadir to end its aridity; 272 were provided, and Marcher and Orc forces can now escort the drovers via Bastion and Necropolis. The Dhomiro of Afar could expand the Herds of Afar, and the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy could trade with the Baron de Hauteville. Frost Eyes received twelve bonds for sixteen drams of realmsroot, a hundred bonds were secured to lure Typhawn, and Thule merchants, the heralds of Callidus and the Hakhandra family also bought bonds. Wayford sold 49 cows at 54 rings; Stockland sold 168 at 48 rings.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, though it held parts of Feroz and Mareave, where the Herds of Afar and the planned Southern Herd lie.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the drovers' route for the Southern Herd runs from the Marches through the Highborn territories of Bastion and Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orcs at Anvil gathered 272 cattle bonds, enough to establish the Southern Herd in Nadir and fund the Shepherd of the Southern Herd, and Orc armies must now help escort the drovers to Mareave.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are blamed for drawing the Summer beast Typhawn into the mortal realm.
n.The Brass Coast: The Dhomiro of Afar had the chance to use a hundred cattle bonds to expand the Herds of Afar, recently re-established with coin from Feroz senator Garviel i Abrira i Erigo, and raise the sinecure's income to 410 rings a season.
n.The Marches: Marcher farmers supplied the 818 bonds traded at Anvil, sold 168 cows at Stockland and 49 at Wayford, and Marcher armies are now needed to escort the drovers south to Mareave.
n.Thule: Thule merchants offered mana crystals for cattle bonds and an economic consortium of Thule bought an unknown number, while the Suaq Wastes plagued by Hayaak's beasts since her attack on the Thule saw a plan to trap Typhawn.
n.Wintermark: The Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq acquired a hundred cattle bonds to lure Typhawn, a wily guardian of Hayaak, into a trap in Sermersuaq, continuing Winterfolk efforts to protect the Suaq.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion lies on the route the drovers and their military escort must take from the Marches to Mareave.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named; the only related item is the Sand Fisher Frost Eyes trading realmsroot for twelve cattle bonds through Misericorde Market.
t.Feroz: The Herds of Afar in Feroz could grow by another hundred head if the Dhomiro of Afar gathered a hundred cattle bonds, raising the sinecure's seasonal income.
t.Mareave: With 272 cattle bonds provided, a Southern Herd can be founded in Mareave once the drovers complete their escorted journey across the Empire.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is home to one of the two cattle markets, where Marcher farmers could sell bonds at prices that rose the fewer cattle were sold.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis lies on the route the drovers and their escort must take before the last leg to Mareave.
t.Sermersuaq: A hundred cattle bonds were secured to lure the Summer beast Typhawn into a trap, offering a chance to slay one of the worst of Hayaak's creatures haunting the territory.
t.Upwold: Upwold is home to one of the two cattle markets, whose sales and fees were to fund improvements to the markets and summer fetes.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The Herds of Afar could be expanded by half again if the Dhomiro of Afar acquired a hundred cattle bonds.
r.Mareave/Nadir: At least two hundred cattle are to be driven to Nadir to form a new great herd that should let local flora and fauna adapt and end the region's aridity.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: A herd of a hundred cattle is to be used to bait Typhawn, which has been savaging the mammoth herds, into a trap in the Suaq Wastes.

If one be gone we carry on.d: After Jarl Haakon Gydasson was defeated at the Winter Solstice, the Tusks and Drakes drove the Jotun from the Ore Hills with help from miners, grateful locals and servants of the Prince with a Thousand Foes. They are a little short of two-fifths of the way to taking the Chalkdowns, but the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch remain in Jotun hands. In Bregasland some forty to fifty thousand Jotun, backed by the Burhfæst garrison and Summer knights, took the Rushes, Grey Fens and North Fens and came eight-tenths of the way to taking Ottermire. The territory is no longer Imperial and Willem Tarne lost his Senate seat. The Lasambrian Corazón looted the Bregasland Breadbasket. A battle opportunity at Sal-Ott Meet offers a chance to halt the final Jotun push.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Military Council sent Imperial heroes to challenge the Druj and eliminate Governor Rahab instead of stopping the Burhfæst's return.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost the Ore Hills and are losing ground in the Chalkdowns, but they still hold the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch. In Bregasland they conquered almost the whole territory, offering the Choice and gaining the support of the Clakes of Beandown.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a number of Navarr traders were killed when the Jotun captured Graven the previous Summer.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies won hard victories in Mournwold, where locals cheered them as liberators, while Bregasland fell almost entirely to the Jotun and lost its senator. The Strong Reeds held together a divided resistance at Ottery.
n.Wintermark: A yegarra raiding band crossed the Westmere into Kallavesa Marsh to plunder Hufi's Garden near Masi, and the Woundbinder of the Mark, Conrald Mystrim, was called on to stop them.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was almost entirely conquered, with only Ottery, the Otterway and the Sallow Way as far as Sal-Ott Meet still resisting. It is no longer Imperial and its Breadbasket granaries were looted, though the Strong Reeds helped the Bregas hide much of their wealth.
t.Kallavesa: Yegarra from Bregasland landed in Kallavesa Marsh aiming for Hufi's Garden. If they reach it, the garden will be devastated and produce half as many herbs until repaired.
t.Liathaven: Ashvale was the staging ground from which tens of thousands of Jotun invaded Bregasland, and Jotun armies there could strike at Mournwold at any moment.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold suffered Jotun raids and a Kalsea yegarra foray repelled by Meade's bounders, sent defenders along the causeway to Ottery, and faces Jotun advance if Bregasland falls.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold is Imperial but far from secure. The Ore Hills were liberated and the Chalkdowns contested, but Jotun champions still hold the Greensward and Farstrider's Watch.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: news of the invasion of Reinos reached the Lasambrians of the Corazón only sporadically.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Burhfæst rose around Graven Rock under the Ice Fishers of Ldansk, and its garrison joined the Jotun invasion that poured through Gravenmarch.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Jotun conquered Grey Fens, which remains sullen. Presenting five captured Corazón pennants could ease that mood.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: North Fens fell to the Jotun, and warbands are now picking their way east from it towards Ottery.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Jotun are eight-tenths of the way to taking Ottermire, where the Bregas resistance and Strong Reeds have fortified Ottery as the last holdout.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Sallow and most of the Rushes fell almost at once, and the resentful Clakes of Beandown welcomed the invaders. An elite kirkja force is now marching north from Sallow towards Ottery.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: A yegarra warband landed here and must pass through Aethelric's Fence on its way to Hufi's Garden. Stopping it there would force it back across the Westmere.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: Mentioned in passing: the castellan of the Burhfæst secured a supply route back to Liath's Ring.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Strong Reeds recently billeted in Meade March recruited defenders here, who marched along the causeway to help hold Ottery.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Refugees fled along Odd's Way to Oddmire, which the Jotun would march on next if Ottery falls. Strong Reeds formerly billeted there recruited defenders for Bregasland.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: A Spring ward and the hares of the Prince with a Thousand Foes aided locals in Alderly, while Einar the Cunning gathers a yegarra warband at the Boar's Hall for the Tusks' general to confront.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Marcher armies pushed into the Chalkdowns and are a little shy of two-fifths of the way to liberating it, though the Jotun still control it.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: Green March is named as a region Jotun armies could strike into from Ashvale at any moment.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Jarl Haakon's allies remain in full control of the Greensward, guarded by veteran champions at Farstrider's Watch.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Ore Hills were liberated, with miners both human and orc lending their supplies and tunnels to the Marchers. Some Marcher orcs sought to enlist, inspired by the voices of their ancestors.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Southmoor to defend Sarcombe, though the region remains exposed to a Jotun strike from Ashvale.

In the flesh.d: The Earl claimed Penni DuBlanche, later Penni the White, defeated it and tested it into his house with the task of making him Monarch of Dawn. It offered to let its favour be magically examined. Invoking hospitality, it named Enchantress de Carsenere guest of honour at a tourney: a grand melee, then a single-elimination contest of eight knights from Anvil against eight of its allied Barrens knights. It added 50 to the Golden Sun's resupply and was winning over some soldiers, though the General could forbid fraternisation. Hayaak challenged the Knight-Protector of Summer to a hunt for one of the Earl's favours, and Tuki of the Little Bones sought to meet Alistair de Vere.

n.Dawn: Dawn's earls rejected the manticore as Dawnish, but the debate continued among the people. The Earl drew support from some Golden Sun soldiers and minor Barrens houses, the Dawnish Assembly had a chance to speak out, and the Knight-Protector of Summer faced Hayaak's challenge.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though a conjunction opened to the Cave of Bones in Skarsind, which they held.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the herald of Jaheris may be the same one recently seen in Sermersuaq, though she denies it.

t.Astolat: A lone herald of Hayaak came to the Castle of Astolat to deliver the Bandit-King's challenge to the Knight-Protector of Summer.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the herald of Jaheris involved may be the one lately seen in Sermersuaq, though she denies it.
t.Skarsind: A conjunction opened to the Cave of Bones in Skarsind, where Tuki of the Little Bones waited to discuss the Earl of the Groves with Alistair de Vere.
t.The Barrens: The Earl of the Groves held its tourney in the Untrod Groves and drew minor Barrens houses into alliance, supplying eight of their knights to face Anvil's champions.

r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Tuki of the Little Bones, a herald of Wise Rangara nesting among ancient bones in the Cave of Bones here, invited Alistair de Vere through a conjunction to talk about the Earl.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Earl had courted minor Dawnish houses here with talk of glory and ambition, and some had begun to accept it as a peer.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Minor Dawnish houses here had been approached by the Earl, and some had begun to treat the manticore as a fellow noble.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The Earl of the Groves called its tourney at Tournament Square by its manse in the heart of the Groves, reachable by a conjunction, with all spectators welcome under guest-law.

Is there anybody out there?.d: Adamant's koboldi offered to help codify Pillars of Adamant, fortify the heliopticon towers and provide beacon plans for Ossium. Barien's heralds will check on the Dawn–Wintermark challenge, and Jaheris extended his fane offer to Wintermark and announced a magicians' tourney for patronage of the Icy Crag. Estavus's heralds cleared Pakaanan's Pass between Skarsind and Sermersuaq. Tharim's knights left Lightsea, spreading nightmares through Calvos and Trivento, camped in Tassato and are bound for Upwold to avenge the herald Obligatus. Sorin's houndmaster offered the Northern Eagle the Elusive quality. Ephisis, Callidus, Zakalwe, Sinokenon, Ylenwe and Sung sought dealings, and greenteeth boggarts plagued Grey Fens and Misericorde.

n.Dawn: Barien's heralds will visit Dawn late on Sunday morning to judge its deeds in his challenge, while Jaheris has offered the fane boon Dawn never built in Dawnguard to Wintermark instead.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named among the threats the proposed beacon at Kostjya's Respite would warn against.
n.Imperial Orcs: Ashborn Trosk raised the declaration and supplied the beggar's lye that saw Pakaanan's Pass cleared, reopening the route from Skarsind to Sermersuaq for Imperial armies.
n.Jotun: The pass the Jotun blocked with Adamant's aid in 383YE is open to Imperial armies again, and greenteeth now plague the Jotun-held Grey Fens.
n.Navarr: Tharim's knights are expected to pass through Miaren after the Spring Equinox on their way to Upwold.
n.The Brass Coast: Tharim's knights broke camp in Lightsea and filled Calvos with nightmares, the Burning Falcon and Red Wind Corsairs met them in Tassato, and Mina i Yashum i Riqueza was asked to gather storytellers for Sung's constellations in Burnish.
n.The League: Tharim's knights brought nightmares to Trivento and camped in Tassato, Astrid Rezia di Tassato was asked to organise constellation makers, Spiral's heliopticon could be fortified, and Claus Friedrich von Holberg must hunt greenteeth in Misericorde.
n.The Marches: Tharim's knights seek vengeance for Obligatus, slain at the Copse of the Bone Birch alongside Marchers including Gerraint Black, and may run riot in Upwold, while Zakalwe's heralds seek views on the Mournwold battle.
n.Urizen: The koboldi offered to help Ioseph codify Pillars of Adamant once Able the Taller finishes his current work, and to fortify the heliopticon towers if Urizen commissions the edifice.
n.Varushka: Dima Vasilyevna Novosad received koboldi plans for a dragon beacon in Bittershore, and the Northern Eagle was offered the new Elusive quality by Sorin's houndmaster Esgyrn.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faces Barien's midpoint check, Jaheris's herald seeks a meeting with its icewalkers and offers a guarded fane in the Suaq Wastes, and Pakaanan's Pass now links Sermersuaq to Skarsind.

t.Astolat: The Northern Eagle rested and resupplied in Astolat while Esgyrn studied the army and devised its proposed Elusive quality.
t.Bregasland: Greenteeth have overrun the deeper Grey Fens, and Orson BogMyrtle is charged with destroying them so households will stay despite the Jotun invasion.
t.Holberg: Ravenous greenteeth are killing people across Misericorde, including Sand Fisher orcs at the Flaxen Pillars.
t.Madruga: Tharim's thousand knights left their camp in Lightsea and marched north through Calvos Sound, leaving terrible dreams behind them.
t.Miaren: Tharim's knights are expected to pass through Miaren after the Spring Equinox on their way to Upwold.
t.Morrow: Morrow's heliopticon tower would become almost impossible to destroy if Urizen commissions the koboldi's reinforcement edifice.
t.Mournwold: Zakalwe's heralds want to hear views on last season's Mournwold battle and fighting alongside heralds of Day, and the miners of the Mourn are among those interested in Jarl Haakon's armour.
t.Ossium: The koboldi have drawn up plans for a dragon-topped beacon in Bittershore that could warn Kostjya's Respite of attack and raise fleet investment in Ossium.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt drew the koboldi to study the Pillars of Adamant enchantment cast there, and its heliopticon tower could be fortified against destruction.
t.Sarvos: Tharim's knights crossed the Spider's Dream into Bocche and brought nightmares to Trivento, and a Sarvos consortium is interested in Jarl Haakon's armour.
t.Segura: Sung has set a field of temporary stars around a night regio in Burnish for Imperial volunteers to shape into constellations for the Night realm.
t.Sermersuaq: Jaheris's herald returned to Rest to court the icewalkers and offer a guarded fane in the Suaq Wastes, while the reopened Pakaanan's Pass links Sermersuaq to Skarsind.
t.Skarsind: Explosions shook western Skarsind as Estavus's heralds cleared Pakaanan's Pass, reopening an army route into Sermersuaq.
t.Spiral: Spiral's heliopticon tower could be made nearly indestructible and kept operating even if the Urizen–League détente collapsed.
t.Tassato: Tharim's knights have camped on Tassato's southern borders, where they met the Burning Falcon and the Red Wind Corsairs and refused to be turned aside.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: a koboldi herald delivered the Ossium beacon blueprints to the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Ossium beacon would face out across the Semmerlak, and greenteeth drag victims into its stagnant pools in Misericorde.
t.Upwold: Obligatus was slain at the Copse of the Bone Birch, and Tharim's vengeful knights are expected to enter Upwold after the Spring Equinox.
t.Zenith: Zenith's heliopticon tower would be protected from destruction if Urizen commissions the koboldi's reinforcement edifice.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Greenteeth burst from stagnant pools to kill fenlanders, and only one person survived the attack on the Breadbasket station at Drowner's Dell.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Greenteeth are killing the vulnerable across the region, and a conjunction to Sacrifice Point lets heroes hunt the clutch that slew Sand Fishers at the Flaxen Pillars.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Tharim's knights marched through Calvos after sunset, filling the town's sleep with nightmares of being buried and bound.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Ashen Knights who had camped in Lightsea for a year broke camp after the Winter Solstice and marched north.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The proposed dragon beacon would stand on Bittershore's shore and, in its grander form, tower over Kostjya's Respite, warning of attacks and guiding Varushkan sailors home.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The knights were allowed over the Spider's Dream toll bridge into Bocche and left Trivento suffering a night of dreams of helplessness.
r.Segura/Burnish: Lights settle like flowers in the Meadow of Dust and Glass, where volunteers will name constellations and craft their lore for Sung's heralds.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Jaheris offers to send creatures to defend the Suaq Wastes if Wintermark builds him a fane there.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Pakaanan's Pass has been blasted clear enough for armies to pass, though there is no road and the foothills remain treacherous.
r.Tassato/Enterio: Tharim's knights marched north along the road into Enterio and made camp on Tassato's southern borders.

It's what we do.d: The civil service provided a magnitude 20 Autumn arcane projection so that all willing citizens could join through a single ritual, and reserved the Senate chamber for the Guild's first meeting and the election of its leader. The Constitutional Court prepared an administrative motion to transfer the power to add potions to Imperial lore to the Guild, and noted that a constitutional motion could also give it the power to interdict potions. League and Freeborn apothecaries offered herbs in return for a statement backing apothecaries' pay. Yerende orcs offered to support a new herbal school if the Druj destroyed Thornsong House. Navarr and Varushkan apothecaries sought interdiction powers covering potions, poisons and drugs.

n.Druj: The Druj encircle Thornsong House, and the page warns that they would destroy it if the Empire's efforts to conceal it failed, as they once destroyed the Halls of Knowledge.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Yerende sept wanted the Guild to focus on service rather than its members' interests, and offered to back a new Apothecaries' Guildhouse under Guild control if Thornsong House were lost. This offer was later superseded by another Wind of Fortune.
n.Navarr: Navarr apothecaries proposed rewriting the manifesto so the Guild would determine the use of potions, poisons and drugs. Control of their Thornsong House could pass to the Guild only through a constitutional motion that the Navarr Assembly could veto.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende devotion to apothecary arts is compared to Urizeni magic, and the Halls of Knowledge, whose Provost was once appointed by Urizeni magicians, is cited as a precedent.
n.Varushka: Varushkan herbalists, worried by the rising trade in foreign narcotics, backed giving the Guild interdiction powers. They offered to investigate substances for the Guild, at ten thrones per season, if the Senate granted those powers.

t.Karov: Herbalists from Karov were among the Varushkans supporting interdiction powers for the Guild and offering to research suspect substances on its behalf.
t.Karsk: Herbalists from Karsk joined those from Karov in backing the Navarr proposal for the Guild to control potions, poisons and drugs.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named, but the page cites the Halls of Knowledge, destroyed by the Druj, as a precedent for Thornsong House.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would cost 10 thrones in upkeep, rather than 12, if built there.
t.Therunin: Thornsong House, the Empire's only potion-research commission, stands in Therunin but is encircled by the Druj and unlikely to operate soon. The Yerende argued that its Thornsinger should be chosen by the Guild.

Keep talking.d: Baroness Katerine Lavasse announced that Josse Argent and fellow priests would meet Silk Farkas, Minister of Historical Research, at the Anvil Library at 12:30 on the Sunday of the Spring Equinox. They would bring artefacts of Suranni victories and wanted a tour of Anvil and introductions to Imperial generals, but no talk of theology. Jotun ghodi under a red banner camped on Gull Isle in West Marsh, Kallavesa. Agnar Tawny Owl asked why the Iron Jarl and Consul Silktongue had proposed it for a Meeting Place, and the ghodi sought tales rather than negotiations until summer. The Imperial Consul would choose who answered. Speaker Morna insisted the Grendel had not worked with the Children of Wrecks in the attack on Redoubt.

n.Grendel: Speaker Morna firmly denied any military alliance with the Children of Wrecks, calling them traitors and suckers, while freely admitting the Grendel had meant to seize Redoubt for its wealth.
n.Jotun: Jotun ghodi led by Agnar Tawny Owl camped on Gull Isle until summer, inviting knowledgeable Imperials to share tales about the proposed Meeting Place while refusing to discuss diplomatic terms. Meanwhile the war continued, with the Jotun conquering Bregasland as the Empire invaded Reinos.
n.Urizen: The Grendel insisted that their failed attack on Urizen's Redoubt had not been coordinated with the Children of Wrecks, though they openly admired the wealth of Cargo.
n.Wintermark: Jotun ghodi camped on Gull Isle, just off Wintermark's coast, and left a note of parley on the Kallavesa shore, alarming local hunters at first but showing no interest in raiding.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name the Bay of Catazar directly; its only apparent link is the Grendel discussion of the Children of Wrecks.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were noted as having conquered Bregasland this season.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz was noted as having been reclaimed by the Empire during the war with the Grendel.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun ghodi camped on Gull Isle off the Kallavesa coast, and their messenger left a note of parley above the tideline after crossing the Kallavesa causeway. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would open to the island on Saturday morning.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Mareave was noted as having been claimed by the Empire from the orcs of the Broken Shore.
t.Redoubt: The Grendel denied that last season's failed attack on Redoubt was a joint effort with the Children of Wrecks, saying they had been as surprised as the Empire to see the wreckers arrive.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Empire was noted as having invaded Reinos this season.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Gull Isle was described as lying near where Kallavesa, Sermersuaq and Skallahn meet.
t.Skallahn: The Jotun ghodi under their tattered red banner crossed the Skallahn causeway at low tide to make camp on Gull Isle.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette was said to lie to the west of Veroigne.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Gull Isle, a small tidal island in West Marsh with traces of old walls, became the camp of Jotun ghodi seeking tales about its proposed use as a Meeting Place, with a Sentinel Gate conjunction opening there at 10:35 on Saturday.

Louder than words.d: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided arranged a Saturday meeting with Ambassador Kindra Surefoot. The Dragons offered three years of peace against the Empire's hoped-for six, and would return half the output of any ceded bourse resource. Ephisis proposed four deals. One would trade food from up to three of Navarr, Highguard, the Marches, Dawn and Varushka for Thule mana, adding a year to the treaty per nation. Orobus offered warlocks to staff Imperial colleges. Caridis offered 50 thrones if the Synod renounces preaching in Otkodov. Thule merchants also sought Marcher cattle bonds. Rejecting the treaty might help bring the Jotun to peace. The Dragons sought an account of the lost Thule of Volham and thanked the Empire for Frekki's death.

n.Dawn: Dawn is one of five nations that could spare food for the proposed Thule trade, gaining 3 thrones per territory in taxes while losing one army's supply. The Reeve of Boar's Market would oversee the trade.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among the nations already at war with the Empire, and as unlikely ever to offer peace terms.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named among the Empire's current enemies, and as unlikely ever to offer peace terms.
n.Highguard: Highguard could commit food to the Thule trade, trading one army's supply for higher taxes and mana. The Cinderpath Custodian would gain ten crystals a season to run it.
n.Jotun: Naomi had judged the Jotun more likely to make peace if the Empire were being weakened by war with the Thule. Rejecting the treaty could therefore be a route to bringing the Jotun to the negotiating table.
n.Navarr: Navarr could supply food to the Thule in exchange for mana and higher taxes, at the cost of one army's supply. The Broker of Treji Wayhouse would manage the trade.
n.Thule: The Dragons demanded Imperial land and offered only three years of peace. They sought food after a devastating famine, offered warlock aid to Imperial colleges and payment for a Synod ban on preaching, and hunted the renegade Nolith Silver-Hand.
n.Urizen: The magicians of Urizen were to vote in the Hall of Worlds on whether Orobus' warlocks should help staff the Doyen of the Spires, in return for reduced upkeep and the Thule receiving copies of codified rituals.
n.Varushka: Two Varushkan regions, Opascari and Mieriada, were named as the land the Dragons want, and many Varushkans resent ceding more territory. Varushka could also supply food to the Thule through the Custodian of the Shchaslyvyy Spile.
n.Wintermark: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark leads the negotiations as Ambassador to Otkodov, while some in Wintermark feel too much land has already been surrendered. Wintermark figures were also thanked for their information about the Agramant's servants.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova's region of Mieriada was one of two the Dragons sought, and it houses the Imperial embassy to Otkodov. The Thule offered to keep the Maze of Zoria under Imperial control if it were ceded.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov is recovering from a famine that killed thousands and left it unable to raise armies without Imperial food. The Dragons wanted any treaty to outlaw preaching the Way there unless the Synod renounced it.
t.Sermersuaq: The Dragons welcomed news that Maarik the Golden Tongue, one of the Agramant's servants threatening Sermersuaq, had been dispatched. They hoped the other followers of the Voice of the Pines would soon follow him.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: Verthandi is not named, though it is among the lands the Dragons have claimed that some Imperial citizens would like to retake.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's region of Opascari was named by the Dragons as land they want ceded, which would put the Hunt of Alderei the Fair under Thule control.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Pen of Vossk of Zenith Ascendant is named as having helped task Ephisis with finding trade opportunities with the Thule.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada was demanded by the Dragons. If ceded, the Night Quarry would pass to the Thule with half its output possibly returned, and the Imperial embassy in its frigid north would then sit in Thule-held land.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: In the opening story, the Whisperer's minions are spreading through Urdur in the wake of the famine, and a Claw of the Dragon sets out from there to hunt the renegade Silverhand.
r.Verthandi/Askja: Mentioned in passing: the region itself is not named; the page refers only to the Warlock Askja, who disavowed the Thule raiders of Volham.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Opascari was one of the two regions the Dragons named. If ceded, the Hunt of Alderei the Fair would be worked by the Thule, with half its production possibly remitted to the Empire.

Love and War.d: After nearly two years the army was almost mustered. Its name was expected to stand apart from the lost Hounds of Glory, and Dawn's weavers would make banners and surcoats once it was chosen. The egregores suggested announcing the decision in the Glory Square before the election of the Senator for the Barrens, to lift spirits. The civil service offered three cost-free qualities: Glorious, with Eleonaris giving its general a triumphant blade each year; Guardian; and Vanguard. House deCassilon of Spiral Castle proposed a fourth, the Magic quality. This required building a Circle of the War-witch in Weirwater, delaying the quality by a season and ending Dawn's ability to support a college of magic.

n.Dawn: Dawn's new army awaited a name and a quality from the Senator for Astolat, a choice between glory, love, conquest or witchery that would shape how Dawnish nobles and yeofolk make war for years.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj appear as the enemy who killed Sir Elegar during the retreat in Therunin, and as the foe Dawn once drove from Ossium.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is not named, though Therunin, a Navarr-held territory, is where Sir Elegar fell fighting with the Golden Sun.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League is not named; the only link is Spiral Castle, which lies in Dawnish Weirwater.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan allies are credited with helping Dawn capture Ossium from the Druj.

t.Astolat: The new Dawnish army was mustering in Astolat, and Astolat's Senator was charged with naming it and choosing its quality. Astolat's artisans of rods, staves and mage armour had ties with Spiral Castle.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is recalled as the land Dawnish and Varushkan armies took from the Druj, and as the setting of Sir Jory's tale of hunting Druj infiltrators.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Spiral Castle in Weirwater rather than the territory of Spiral itself.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is cited as the Hounds of Glory's legacy, now part of Dawn, and the election of its Senator was suggested as the moment to announce the army's name.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Sir Elegar is said to have fallen in Therunin, fighting with the Golden Sun during the retreat from the Druj.
t.Weirwater: House deCassilon of Spiral Castle in Weirwater proposed building a Circle of the War-witch there, a 25 white granite and 75 crown edifice that would give the new army the Magic quality.

r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: The proposed Circle of the War-witch is listed as sited near Spiral Castle in Weirmoor, with the castle providing hospitality and upkeep if it is built.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The deCassilon proposal describes building the Circle of the War-witch, a stone duelling ground ringed by a dozen monoliths, in Wickmoor in the vale below Spiral Castle.

Our eyes in Spiral.d: The Vigilant sorted the Black Plateau's dangers into naifs, the Lost and the enemy. They urged close watch over the Oblivion Sentinel, more resources for that office, and enmity with Lashonar, the Muse of Fire, Azoth and the Whisper Gallery. They proposed Oblivion's Edge, a fortification around the Plateau in Screed, as an opportunity open until Spring Equinox 388YE. In Apulus, their pilgrim Victo von Temeschwar vanished while infiltrating a suspected Grendel ring and was later found paranoid and maddened. A Sentinel Gate conjunction gives the Voice of Vigilance a chance to save Victo. Caela's rebels are abiding by the treaty and have rebuffed the Grendel. Further Vigilant are still investigating Redoubt.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant's search of Astolat found no active cultists of Agramant.
n.Druj: The Vigilant warn that if southern Zenith ever fell to the Druj, they might raid Spiral to target the Black Plateau, as the Iron Helms once did. The proposed Oblivion's Edge fortification is meant partly to deter such a strike.
n.Grendel: The Grendel are suspected of running an espionage ring in Apulian, and their approaches to Caela's rebels have been firmly rebuffed. The Vigilant expect any Grendel bid to retake Spiral to come as a swift surprise attack.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant's mandate drew on the true liao consecration of the damaged basilica in Bastion in Berechiah's name.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Grendel armies would have to pass through Imperial Orc-controlled Mareave to contest Spiral.
n.The League: League citizens in Spiral live in Apulian, a booming city the Vigilant see as fertile ground for Grendel spies. One League pilgrim, Victo von Temeschwar, lost their senses while trying to infiltrate the ring. The Vigilant also warn that any League settlement nearer Screed could be disastrous.
n.Urizen: Most Urizeni rebels in Spiral have been mollified, and Urizeni magicians now share knowledge of the Block with League neighbours. Caela's Silver Flame holds Cinion under the treaty but poses no active threat. The Vigilant are still investigating Redoubt.

t.Astolat: The Vigilant's search for cultists of Agramant here found none currently active, which the page treats as a success.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant mandate took advantage of the true liao consecration of the damaged basilica in Bastion.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that Grendel armies would have to come through Mareave, described as Imperial Orc-controlled, to contest Spiral.
t.Redoubt: Followers of Berechiah, sent by a Summer 386YE Assembly mandate, are still seeking threats here. Their report is expected by Summer or by Autumn at the latest.
t.Spiral: After a year of watching, the Vigilant found no active threats at the Black Plateau or among the rebels, though the Plateau remains deeply dangerous. They did uncover a likely Grendel espionage ring in Apulus and proposed the Oblivion's Edge fortification to contain the Plateau.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Vigilant pilgrim Victo von Temeschwar is from here, orphaned when the Vyig burned their parents' business.
t.Zenith: Zenith is now fully back in Urizeni hands, but the Vigilant warn that losing its southern part to the Druj could open a path for a raid on Spiral's Black Plateau.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Mentioned in passing: Ankra is named as a home of Urizeni rebels and as bordering the spire of the Lost Spire of the Black Plateau.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: a companion Wind of Fortune about damming the River Doubt in Apstrus is listed, and Zie of the Perfect Morning's offer of protection is tied to that plan.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Vigilant found evidence of a Grendel espionage ring in the city of Apulian, where their undercover pilgrim Victo was found maddened. A conjunction to The Cellar Below safehouse offers a chance to restore Victo and learn what they uncovered.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Ceded by treaty to Caela of the Silver Flame, Cinion's rebels have disavowed the violent Spire of Black Glass and rejected Grendel approaches. The Vigilant report no active threat there for now.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary is one of the regions bordering the abandoned spire taken over by the Lost Spire of the Black Plateau.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Black Plateau at the heart of Screed shows no active threats and may calm within ten to twenty years, but remains incredibly dangerous. The Vigilant propose building Oblivion's Edge here to secure the passes, keep naifs out and defend against direct attack.
r.Temeschwar/Vargat: Mentioned in passing: Victo's parents ran Vargataia Delicacies, a business selling the foods of the Vargat region.

Outside the wall.d: Naomi found few displaced Varushkans beyond those unhomed by Cold Sun and the Schlacta of Rot, and many were already in Delev. She proposed warding the Little Boyar's Welcome (20 mithril, 60 crowns), which would raise Karov's taxation by 6 thrones. She also proposed a Great Market at Delev (50 white granite, 150 crowns) and a Golden Bee Assayer's Office sinecure (14 mithril, 42 crowns). A Synod mandate could turn miners away from Temeschwar. Oksana Lyava Pinavora offered 900 thrones towards buying the Hunt of Alderei the Fair for Varushka. The bees of Duzekani remain missing, possibly for supernatural reasons, and magicians suggested a further appraisal or dealings with eternals. None of these proposals is time sensitive.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: folk from Dawn were among those Naomi consulted.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the concedence of Miechernya is recalled as the price of securing Otkodov's aid against the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step is among the armies honoured on the Little Boyar's Welcome mural for defending Delev from Cold Sun.
n.The League: Temeschwar is cast as Delev's great rival, and its Assayer's Guild is resented for drawing Varushkan metal trade into the League. A proposed mandate would cut Temeschwar's taxation by 2 thrones, and Holberg is held up as the exemplar of a true city.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Meade is cited as a small city Delev might come to match.
n.Thule: Thule merchants trade crystal mana in Delev but were reluctant to commit with the Otkodov treaty due for renegotiation. Varushkans fear further regions, perhaps Opascari or Mieriada, might be traded to the orcs for peace.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen merchants trade in Delev, and Urizen pilgrims to the Maze of Zoria recalled Clytemnestra's threat to destroy the Citadel Guard.
n.Varushka: The proposals offer Varushka a chance to make Delev a fortified, prosperous rival to Temeschwar and to keep its metal trade at home. Oksana Lyava Pinavora urged Varushkans to pool funds to buy the Hunt of Alderei the Fair, while worries persist over the vanished bees and further territorial concessions to the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark merchants travel to Delev, and Kalpaheim is named as a city Delev might rival.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its city of Kalpaheim is cited as a benchmark for Delev's possible growth.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was consulted as the exemplar of a true city, and its splendid defences were held up as a model for Delev's walls.
t.Karov: Karov is the focus of the appraisal. Warding Delev's walls, building the Great Market and founding the Golden Bee Assayer's Office would together raise its taxation by up to 12 thrones and boost its businesses, while the missing bees threaten its farms and trade.
t.Karsk: The region of Krevsaty was ceded to the Thule seven years ago. Karsk's proxy senator is praised for having provided all the mithril and funds for a new army up front.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not described directly, and appears only through the wider references to other nations' armies and merchants.
t.Miekarova: Miechernya was conceded to Otkodov, displacing Varushkans, and Mieriada is rumoured to be at risk of being traded away in a new peace.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its town of Meade is cited as a small city Delev might come to equal.
t.Ossium: Two regions of Ossium are claimed by the Thule, which chafes with Varushkans. The Vale of the Sunless Depths beneath a town there is cited in the argument over Imperial bourse seats.
t.Otkodov: The five-year peace treaty with Otkodov, lucrative but costly in ceded land, expires this year. Varushkans fear its renegotiation may cost more regions.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's dominance of Varushkan metal trade and the old dispute over the Eternal Shafts of Time fuel Delev's rivalry. A proposed Synod mandate would strip it of the Delev Market stream and 2 thrones of taxation.
t.The Semmerlak: Delev guards the road from the Semmerlak, and the Great Market would add a rank to the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak's ministry.
t.Volodmartz: Cold Sun's scions destroyed vales in Volodmartz, unhoming many, and its region of Opascari is rumoured to be at risk of being traded to the Thule.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in the Battle of the Weirwater Gate, fought at Delev, whose ruined gate was built into the new walls.

r.Karov/Duzekani: Delev lies in Duzekani, and every proposal would be built there, adding to its taxation and protecting sites such as the Iron Roundtower. Its bees have vanished since Cold Sun's attack and have still not returned.
r.Karov/Kamienczka: People fled the dead of the Schlacta of Rot here and no longer feel safe in isolated settlements, and there are anxious reports of fewer bees as spring approaches.
r.Karov/Skoremujac: Folk displaced by the Schlacta of Rot, or fearful in remote vales, would welcome new defended homes, and locals report seeing fewer bees.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Anxious reports from Wieliczka suggest there are fewer bees as spring approaches, raising fears that Duzekani's problem is spreading.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Its ceding to the Thule seven years ago forced Varushkans to migrate south or remain as subjects of the Dragons. Most who left are now settled elsewhere.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Its concedence displaced Varushkans such as the woodcutter Vasily's family, who later fled the scions south and fell on hard times.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada holds a bourse seat rumoured to be at risk of being traded to Otkodov. Oksana hopes Varushkan ownership of the Hunt and Quarry would protect it.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Opascari holds a bourse seat rumoured to be a possible bargaining chip for peace with Otkodov, which Oksana's offer seeks to guard against.
