Raise Fourth Highborn Army.d: The motion drew on an opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune 'The war of thorns and flowers'. Its cost was cut from 200 to 80 mithril and from 600 to 240 crowns because each of Highguard's generals had received a hallowed banner as regalia. The new army's general would carry the hallowed banner Ever Forward. Work took six months. Asael gave most of the mithril and money over two seasons, with smaller donations from Naomi of Felix Watch and several other citizens. Once complete, the general of the Pilgrim's Defiance was to be chosen for the first time at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, by unanimous decision of the Highborn senators, for a shortened term of one season.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a fourth army, the Pilgrim's Defiance, at a much lower cost because of the hallowed banners given to its generals. Its senators were to choose the new general unanimously at the Autumn Equinox 387YE.

t.Casinea: The new Highborn army was raised in Casinea, whose senator proposed the motion.

Raise Second Urizen Army.d: Proposed by Zenith and seconded by Segura, the motion raised the Argent Sword as Urizen's second army in Redoubt, following the opportunity in the A box for a sword Wind of Fortune. It cost 300 mithril and 900 crowns and took six months. After the Spring Equinox the costs were met by contributors including Able the Taller of Sarangrave Reforged, Bartimaeus, Herminius of the House of the Wanderer, Aulus Warcaster and Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was, with single crowns from two others. Once complete, the army's general was to be chosen for the first time at the Summer Solstice 387YE by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators, serving a shortened term to the Winter Solstice 387YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen gained a second army, the Argent Sword, whose first general was to be appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators at the Summer Solstice 387YE.

t.Redoubt: The Argent Sword was raised in Redoubt, which became the home of Urizen's new second army.

Raise Third Navarr Army.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Weirwater. It followed the opportunity described in The first shot wind of fortune. The army takes twelve months to raise. Rare materials could replace mithril, and the support of the Ethengraw cut the amount needed for each wain to 36 ingots or measures. Contributions came in from Spring to Winter Solstice 387YE from many individual Navarr, from the City of Gold and Lead and from the Artisans of Treji. Mandates at the Summer Solstice brought support from citizens of Dawn, the Marches, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs. Once the army is complete, its general will be elected by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Dawn supported the motion through a mandate enacted by The Fool of Glory, and provided 10 wains of mithril.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: citizens of the Imperial Orcs supported the motion through a mandate enacted by Skywise Gralka at the Summer Solstice 387YE.
n.Navarr: Navarr gains a third Imperial army, raised largely through donations from its own people, and its senators will elect that army's general by unanimous decision once it is complete.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Varushka supported the motion through a mandate enacted by Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, and provided 10 wains of mithril.

t.Hercynia: The new Navarr army is to muster in Treji in the Glen of Shadows, Hercynia, and the Artisans of Treji contributed mithril towards raising it.

Ratify Thule Treaty Spring 387YE.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Karsk, the treaty was to take effect at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE, when the previous peace treaty expired. The Empire would cede Mieriada to Otkodov, send food sufficient for two armies (initially from Navarr and the Marches, changeable by the Senate) and outlaw preaching the Way of Virtue to Otkodov's citizens there. In return Otkodov would provide half the Night Quarry's production as an Imperial bourse seat, pay for the food in taxes and mana crystals, and allow continued Imperial custody of the Maze of Zoria. Both sides agreed a five-year peace. Nikolai "The Butcher" Petravich sought a Synod veto, which failed.

n.Navarr: Navarr was named as one of the first two nations obliged to send food to Otkodov, in return for 3 extra thrones of taxation a season in its territories and 10 mana crystals.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov were to gain Mieriada, Imperial food shipments and a ban on Virtue preaching to their citizens, while sharing the Night Quarry's output and paying for the food.
n.Varushka: Varushka was set to lose the Mieriada region of Miekarova to Otkodov, under a treaty proposed by Miekarova's own senator and seconded by Karsk.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova was to lose its region of Mieriada to Otkodov when the treaty took effect at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov was to receive Mieriada and Imperial food, with Virtue preaching to its citizens outlawed, while sharing the Night Quarry's production and allowing Imperial custody of the Maze of Zoria.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada was to be ceded to Otkodov at the end of the Summer Solstice 387YE, with Otkodov agreeing to maintain its current treatment of Imperial citizens who chose to stay in ceded lands.

Speak to me.d: Skathe offered formal parley to the Winter Archmage, the Grandmaster of the Celestial Arch and the Custodian of the Bleak Tower. Her gifts for the Sarangrave depend on a sincere show of hatred for the Druj. The Invisible Hand sent assessors into the Empire and Otkodov. Cathan Canae will send Volstann to discuss the frozen citadels and Eoradal. Sadogua's heralds will hold an informal celebration, and he will privately consult the Unfettered Mind about the Lyceum's wards. Ylenwe declined parley but offered a ritual to harmonise Skarsind's white wood and help with Solen's Doubt. Ossegrahn will discuss watering Mareave, and offers lasting protection for Peakedge Stead if the Conclave removes two rituals from Imperial lore through a power of Remorse.

n.Druj: Skathe offers gifts for the Sarangrave if the Empire convinces her of its hatred for the Druj. Ossegrahn warns that the Druj will destroy Peakedge Stead unless his demands are met.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named. Their only link is through Mareave, where eternals discuss Imperial Orc plans to bring fresh water to the territory.
n.Imperial Orcs: Cathan Canae asks the Legion Engineer to explain how the Orcs will hold Eoradal. Ossegrahn wants Orcs at his parley to discuss watering Mareave and peace with the Brine Turtles, and Ylenwe offers a ritual to harmonise Skarsind's white wood.
n.Navarr: Ossegrahn offers lasting protection for Peakedge Stead in Therunin at the price of a power of Remorse. Sadogua invites Navarr magicians to discuss threatened magical places in Therunin, and Skathe speaks of the scions of Terunael's bitterness towards the Druj.
n.The League: Skathe welcomes the Archmage's admission that events in Holberg and Sarvos were the work of Zephaniah's Lament, not her. Both Ylenwe and Ossegrahn take an interest in plans to dam Solen's Doubt in Spiral.
n.The Marches: Sadogua invites Marcher magicians to speak with his apprentices about their studies. He warns that this is their last season of easy access to the Well of Shadows before he seeks a new scholar at the Summer Solstice.
n.Thule: The City of Gold and Lead has sent agents into Otkodov, drawing on its good relations with the Thule to pursue the Autumn Archmage's request.
n.Urizen: The masters of the Celestial Arch and Bleak Tower are invited to Skathe's parley. Cathan Canae questions why three defenders of Redoubt were singled out, and Ossegrahn is sceptical about a fane in Redoubt and the Urizen request about mana-site food.
n.Varushka: Varushkan members of the Unfettered Mind are warned to be very cautious at Sadogua's Lyceum meeting. The eternal is still angry over the Towers of Zulgan Tash.
n.Wintermark: A Wintermark civil servant received Skathe's message. Sadogua's heralds hope to meet the Wintermark magicians responsible for a recent splendid enchantment.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Skathe refers to past events in 'enlightened Holberg', which she says were caused by Zephaniah's Lament, and offers to clear up any doubts about them.
t.Mareave: Ylenwe cautions about the costs of bringing water to the arid territory but judges the plans gentle. Ossegrahn offers to help with founts in north-eastern Mareave.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not named. The page's Varushkan content concerns a warning to Varushkan Unfettered Mind magicians and Sadogua's anger over the Towers of Zulgan Tash.
t.Otkodov: Assessors, brokers and planners from the City of Gold and Lead have been dispatched into Otkodov to speak with the Thule on the Autumn Archmage's behalf.
t.Redoubt: Cathan Canae asks why three particular defenders of Redoubt merit special note. Ossegrahn is prepared, if sceptical, to discuss the Urizen notion of a fane there.
t.Sarangrave: Skathe has prepared gifts to bring weal to the Sarangrave's inhabitants, conditional on a sincere show of Imperial hatred for the Druj. Ossegrahn suggests Peakedge Stead could become a sanctuary for those fighting the vallorn there.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Skathe refers to past events in 'beautiful Sarvos', attributing them to Zephaniah's Lament.
t.Skarsind: Ylenwe offers a way to harmonise the warped white wood. A tree from its edge is to be brought to the Imperial regio and sung through all seven modes using magical chimes, rendering the dangerous Day magic inert.
t.Spiral: Ylenwe has sent heralds to Solen's Doubt to help with damming it. Ossegrahn asks that a representative of Spiral attend his parley to discuss releasing and channelling its waters.
t.Therunin: Ossegrahn's protection of Peakedge Stead and his Houses of Healing will fail within a day of the Equinox unless the Conclave removes Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers Its Youth from lore. Sadogua invites talk of the territory's threatened magical places.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named. The only Marches content is Sadogua's invitation to Marcher magicians and his note about the Well of Shadows.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the herald of the City of Gold and Lead thanks Vossk of Zenith Ascendant for her concise missive.

r.Mareave/Eoradal: Cathan Canae wants to hear, through Volstann, how the Imperial Orcs intend to hold Eoradal and the building there, and why they seek her aid rather than the Dragon Beneath the Mountain's.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Ossegrahn wishes to discuss plans to channel the released waters of Solen's Doubt into Icarion.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: Apstrus is not named. Spiral's part in the page concerns damming Solen's Doubt, detailed in the Damming the Doubt wind.

Stars and sigils.d: Beast attacks and unexplained brawling spread from Sermersuaq into Skarsind, Hahnmark and Hercynia, and more faintly further south. The Mystics of Ishal offered the Ravenseer three mutually exclusive paths. A Night enchantment filled Kallavesa with feasting. All seventy villagers of Zurrah in Ossium were found devoured, with their skulls and clothes missing. The Grand Conjunction made older army and fleet projections defunct, though they could be exchanged for mana, and it empowered several personal enchantments. The Claw stirred violent urges. The Penumbral Veil persisted over most of the Empire, and Sir Gaeris's Twisted Torc enriched the Barrens. Other omens included a doom-bell in the Bay of Catazar, vision-dreams in Casinea and a mysterious tavern in Mournwold.

n.Dawn: Dawn saw unexplained animal attacks in the wild places of Astolat and Weirwater. All four of its territories lay under the shroud, and Sir Gaeris's use of the Twisted Torc brought prosperity to the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, which Grendel held, is listed among the shrouded territories, where it is described as the Brass Coast's reclaimed land.
n.Highguard: Liao dreams in Casinea took the form of fragmentary past-life visions linked to a dramaturgical confluence, and Bastion, Casinea and Reikos remained shrouded.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind was caught up in the wave of beast attacks and violence, and the largest wolf pack seen since the orcs gained their homeland attacked the Great Herd in Estermark.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Jotun were feeling the spreading violence, and their territory of Bregasland was listed among those under the shroud.
n.Navarr: Hercynia suffered pronounced beast attacks, and a dire bear struck travellers in Miaren's Goldglades. Navarr-owned resources in the Barrens also shared in the cheaper upgrades there.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman, Segura and the reclaimed Feroz lay under the Penumbral Veil, leaving their night skies strange and unfamiliar.
n.The League: All five League cities remained shrouded, with Sarvos veiled over three times more strongly than elsewhere. Temeschwar saw unexplained animal attacks, though not from rats.
n.The Marches: A mysterious Wintermark-style tavern, the Crow's Rest, appeared in the Ore Hills of Mournwold, and Mitwold and Upwold remained shrouded.
n.Thule: The Thule would not say whether the violence had reached Otkodov, and rumour in Ossium blamed Thule cannibals for the slaughter at Zurrah.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the attempted raid on Redoubt is cited in the tale of the doom-bell, and Urizen lore and the Doyen of the Spires are referenced elsewhere.
n.Varushka: The whole village of Zurrah in Ossium was found slaughtered and devoured, western Karov saw animal attacks, and Karsk, Miekarova and Ossium remained shrouded.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was the heart of the spreading beast attacks, the Ravenseer was offered a choice of three tasks for the Mystics of Ishal, and Kallavesa enjoyed a season of enchanted feasting.

t.Astolat: The wild places of Astolat saw unexplained animal attacks as the Spring Equinox approached, and the territory remained under the shroud.
t.Bastion: Bastion remained under the Penumbral Veil, its night skies showing displaced stars and odd lights.
t.Bay of Catazar: A bell was heard tolling above or beneath the bay's dark waters, filling sailors with dread and seeming to herald, or avert, shipwrecks.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland remained under the Penumbral Veil that persisted across most of the Empire.
t.Casinea: Liao dedication dreams in Casinea became snippets of past-life visions, some unknown to the Echoes, and the territory remained shrouded.
t.Feroz: Feroz remained under the Penumbral Veil, where it was described as the Brass Coast's reclaimed territory.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark suffered pronounced attacks by beasts and mundane animals, along with outbreaks of deadly brawling.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia was among the four territories worst hit by maddened beasts and sudden violence, and it remained shrouded.
t.Holberg: Holberg remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Kallavesa: A Night enchantment filled Kallavesa with dreams of feasting and good company and left lasting benefits for its residents. It may also explain why the north of the territory was spared the beast attacks.
t.Karov: The wild places of western Karov saw unexplained animal attacks as the Spring Equinox approached.
t.Karsk: Karsk remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Miaren: Northern Miaren was not spared the attacks: a dire bear struck travellers in Goldglades. The territory remained shrouded.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Mournwold: A mysterious tavern called the Crow's Rest appeared out of the fog on a rocky hill, welcoming those who accepted its hospitality.
t.Ossium: All seventy villagers of Zurrah were found slain and gnawed, with their skulls and clothes missing, and folk across Ossium were urged to secure their gates against strangers.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: it was unknown whether the spreading violence had reached Otkodov, and the Thule were not saying.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the attempted raid on Redoubt is noted as the time the Lighthouse at Nikephoros fell and the bell-tolling grew stronger.
t.Reikos: Reikos remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos lay under the strongest shroud in the Empire, more than three times as powerful as those over other territories.
t.Segura: Segura remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was the source of the escalating beast attacks and violence. A captured husk from the Gullet awaited vivisection by an Unfettered Mind magician, and the territory remained shrouded.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind suffered pronounced beast attacks and violence, including a massive wolf pack's assault on the Great Herd.
t.Spiral: Spiral remained under the Penumbral Veil, and the page points to a separate wind on odd dramaturgical events in the city.
t.Tassato: Tassato remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar saw unexplained animal attacks in its wild places, though rats there were unaffected, and the territory remained shrouded.
t.The Barrens: Sir Gaeris's use of the Twisted Torc spread prosperity across the Barrens, making most personal resources there cheaper to upgrade until the Autumn Equinox. The territory remained shrouded.
t.Upwold: Upwold remained under the Penumbral Veil, leaving its night skies strange and unfamiliar.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater saw unexplained animal attacks in its wild places, and the territory remained shrouded.

r.Miaren/Goldglades: A dire bear attacked travellers in Goldglades, leaving two dead and half a dozen badly injured; Roadwardens prevented worse.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: The Crow's Rest, a mysterious tavern with a Wintermark feel, appeared high on a rocky hill in the Ore Hills.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The slaughtered village of Zurrah lay on the edges of the Bonewood, and nearby communities were urged to take extra care.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Consternation spread in the Galath Fields when Zurrah's usual Spring trade caravan never arrived, prompting the investigation.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Zurrah, whose villagers were found devoured, stood on the edges of the Webwood.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Mystics of Ishal found an isolated hall here holding vellum records of the runesmith Storm's Folly and their study of the artoks.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Heroes hunting the Suaq Wastes each season helped keep losses to a minimum as maddened beasts took hunters from the Hall of the Hunters.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: The largest wolf pack seen since the orcs gained their homeland attacked the Great Herd. It was driven off under the Shepherd of the Great Herd, but sporadic attacks continued.

The hard way.d: Lucati's sermon, delivered in the Atrium of Golden Light, spread across the Empire through pilgrims and Sarvos pamphlets. Drawing on work at the Great Library of Hacynian, it argued that destroying the vallorn was achievable within a decade if the Empire united. The General Assembly could enact a mandate, sending a named priest with 250 liao, urging the faithful to focus on the vallorn above all else. Only with a greater majority would it create new opportunities against the vallorn. The price was steep: no new opportunities against the Druj or for converting the Asaveans, and muted appraisals on those subjects. Only Lucati could submit or amend the mandate.

n.Druj: If the mandate passed, the Empire would stop seeking ways to bring down the Druj or invade the Mallum, leaving their evil to fester until the vallorn was destroyed, even though the Druj were already pushing the Empire back on the Eastern front.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the Empire was then fighting, alongside the Druj and the Jotun.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the foes the Empire was then fighting, alongside the Druj and the Grendel.
n.Navarr: The sermon praised the Navarr's centuries of walking the trods against the vallorn and offered the prospect of the final victory that had eluded them for nearly a thousand years, if the Empire united behind the mandate.
n.The League: The sermon came from the Archbishop of Capodomus in the League's own cathedral, invoked the League's mantra "nothing great without cost", and was spread by Sarvos printers alongside the League assembly's recent words of support for the fight against the vallorn.
n.Urizen: Urizen's priests declared they would not support a mandate that did not reflect the clear will of the General Assembly, which is why a greater majority was required.
n.Varushka: Varushkan priests declared they would not support a mandate that did not reflect the clear will of the General Assembly, which is why a greater majority was required.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia was named as a territory in the grip of the vallorn that great armies would need to free if the Empire committed to the mandate's ambition.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, was named as a territory in the grip of the vallorn that great armies would need to free if the Empire took up the vallorn as its goal.
t.Sarvos: The truly consecrated Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos drew pilgrims from across the Empire and beyond, hosted the sermon, and saw its printers spread the speech as pamphlets, while also housing Empress Giselle's completed resting place.

The play that came to Apulian.d: Residents of Apulian found themselves lost in unfamiliar streets, always ending up at some thrilling performance, as the city reverberated with Night magic. Plays drawing on the six personae drew rave reviews, personae appeared where they should not, and citizens felt inspired by them. Heated debate between astronomancers and dramaturgists turned to fruitful cooperation, producing two rival proposals: Salina of the White Harbour's Academy of Dramaturgical Arts, or Sean de Apulian's larger University, a college of magic with a Virtuoso of Apulus title, both available until Summer Solstice 387YE. Separately, Actius of the Deathless Cave pressed again for the Chamber of Euphony, now slightly costlier, as the Dancer grew discordant and insistent.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Dancer fell silent after Spiral was lost to the Grendel five decades ago, and the orc Sean de Apulian is described as a former Grendel.
n.The League: League dramaturgy enjoyed a striking renaissance in its city of Apulian, and the League was offered a University of Dramaturgical Arts that would use its capacity for a college of magic, along with a Virtuoso of Apulus title, while the League Assembly's long-backed fane for Sung remained unbuilt.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's modest size is compared to the Marcher town of Meade.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians living in Apulian joined League colleagues to study the phenomena and could gain from the proposed University, which could speed the Doyen of the Spires' codification work, while Actius of the Deathless Cave pressed the Empire to build Sung's fane.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a doctor from Holberg is described fighting off two bravos with a parasol after imagining themselves as the Captain.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is said to be not much bigger than Meade.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a critic's barb about the play The DOOM that came to Sarvos is quoted, and the Academy might teach theatre beyond the classical Sarvosi style.
t.Spiral: Spiral's capital became the focus of Night-touched dramaturgical wonders and a magical debate, with opportunities for an Academy or University of Dramaturgy, and League and Urizen citizens with resources there could draw on the personae for strength this summit.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is invoked through a narrator's quip, the play Three Princes of Tassato and the playwright Antonio di Tassato.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Mentioned in passing: wits claim one can cross Apulian in the time it takes to stroll round Holmauer Park.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: a companion wind of fortune on damming the River Doubt in Apstrus is listed as further reading.
r.Spiral/Apulus: In Apulus people got lost in new streets full of performances, personae seemed to walk among them, and the city was proposed as the home of a dramaturgical academy or university and of Sung's Chamber of Euphony.

The shape of things to come.d: Following the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge in Mareave, the Conclave endowed 25 mana to the Silver Tears, wealthy Freeborn from Kahraman, Madruga and Segura, to plan a Silver Chalice lodge of equal scale in Madruga. They rejected Crucible and Siroc Bayou as unstable, Torres and the Quiet Grasses as too remote, Free Landing because of the Children of Wrecks, and Calvos Sound as already crowded. They chose Quzar, meeting place of the hakima, where the once-cursed caravanserai well flows again. The commission would cost 40 white granite, 40 weirwood, 20 mithril and 60 Crowns over two seasons. It would provide mana, a great hospital, vital honey and herbs, and fewer army casualties in four territories, and would create the Hakima of the Rippling Marshes. Further lodges must wait.

n.Grendel: Grendel held Feroz and Mareave that season; if built, the lodge would cut casualties for Imperial armies fighting in Feroz by a tenth. Mareave is named as the site of the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn patrons proposed to host the Silver Chalice's grand lodge at Quzar, drawing on the hakima and their kohan. If built, it would reduce Imperial army casualties across the Coast and create the elected Freeborn post of Hakima of the Rippling Marshes to support exploration of Crucible and the Bayou.

t.Feroz: If the Well of Life were completed, Imperial armies fighting in Feroz would suffer a tenth fewer casualties each season, as healers travelled the roads from Quzar.
t.Kahraman: Some of the Silver Tears' founders came from Kahraman, and Imperial armies fighting there would lose a tenth fewer casualties once the lodge was complete.
t.Madruga: Madruga was chosen for the Silver Chalice's grand lodge, which would boost its herb gardens and bring vital honey and ilium from its transformed regions and bay. It would also field a great hospital and cut casualties for Imperial armies fighting there.
t.Mareave: Mareave hosts the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge under construction, the model whose scale the Silver Chalice's plans were to match. Its completion is one trigger allowing the Conclave to seek a further lodge.
t.Segura: Some of the Silver Tears' founders came from Segura, and Imperial armies fighting there would suffer a tenth fewer casualties once the lodge was built.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound was considered as a site but rejected because a great deal of other work, including the Professors' new city, is already proposed there.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Crucible was discounted as a building site for fear the Night-touched marsh might transform or swallow it, but the lodge would let the grandmaster buy its vital honey. The new Hakima would be expected to support Freeborn exploring it.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing was ruled out as a site because it is currently controlled by the Children of Wrecks.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Well of Life would be built at the abandoned Jayyani Caravanserai outside Quzar, whose cursed well now flows again. The opportunity ends if Lightsea leaves Imperial control.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Grasses were judged less appealing than the coast and passed over as a site.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Siroc Bayou was discounted as a site because of the unstable Night-wrought changes, though its vital honey would be sold through the lodge. Its exploration would be supported by the new Hakima of the Rippling Marshes.
r.Madruga/Torres: Mentioned in passing: Torres was judged less appealing than the busy coast and passed over as a site.

To hold death's hand in mine.d: With no Imperial army left in Therunin, the Navarr assembly told those who could not fight to flee to Reikos, the Barrens and northern Urizen. Druj hosts poured from Eastring and East Ashes and took the Lower and Upper Tarn Valley and Peakedge Song. The Senate's new Apothecaries' Guild could not use its antidote on the poisoned Lower Tarn and spent its ten thrones aiding refugees and defenders instead. Thornsong House vanished behind a warding fog. Ossegrahn's bramble wall saved Peakedge Stead and the Houses of Healing for now, but it will fail without action by the Conclave and Senate. Using goetic magic and treasures taken from Return, the Tainted Basilisk woke the vallorn of Tharunind, which now spreads miasma towards neighbouring lands.

n.Dawn: Dawn was among the nations that opened their doors to Therunin's refugees. Its Barrens face Druj tortured souls advancing on Hope's Rest, and Navarr fear the waking vallorn may eventually threaten Dawnish people.
n.Druj: The Druj conquered all of Therunin except Sweetglades and Greenheart, slaughtering or enslaving those in their path. They were halted only at Peakedge Stead, where a force waits outside Ossegrahn's failing hedge, and the Tainted Basilisk roused the vallorn of Tharunind.
n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly asked the chapters of Reikos to shelter Navarr and Great Forest Orc refugees, and many from Peakedge Stead took sanctuary in High Chalcis. Highborn support had helped find the antidote to the Lower Tarn poison.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun's continued hold on Liathaven, which they have renamed Ashvale, is cited as the reason Therunin's people doubt they will ever return.
n.Navarr: The Navarr lost Therunin, and with it their capacity to support armies fell from six to five. Their assemblies urged evacuation, and almost all stridings and many steadings fled while those who stayed died buying time. Peakedge Stead, the Houses of Healing and Thornsong House now stand alone in enemy hands.
n.Urizen: Northern Urizen took in Navarr refugees, but vallorn miasma has appeared in the foothills of Peregro and Altis, and a vallornspawn horde threatens the Spire of the Canticle. A Spring pulse also swept along the trods of Redoubt and Zenith.
n.Varushka: The undying remnants of Varushka's Iron Helms ravaged the Druj in Eastring, but their bound winter spirits overwhelmed what remained of the soldiers. The Navarr assembly honoured Alderai the Fair and the Iron Helms for their sacrifice.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: held up as a warning, since years after similar assurances it remains under Jotun control and has been renamed Ashvale.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: named by the Navarr assembly as one of the places to which the young, old and weak might be guided to safety.
t.Morrow: Vallorn miasma has been spotted in Morrow's northern foothills, and a horde led by heralds of Yaw'nagrah marches on the Spire of the Canticle. Its chaos-fruit forests will yield two extra fruit.
t.Redoubt: The pulse of Spring magic from the rousing vallorn struck along Redoubt's trods, and Redoubt's senator had raised the motion creating the Apothecaries' Guild. Therunin's defences had already weakened when the League engineers left for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Reikos became a key refuge, with chapters opening their doors and many from Peakedge Stead fleeing to High Chalcis. The Druj impaled stragglers along the road there, and its chaos-fruit forests gain two extra fruit from the Spring pulse.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: cited as a place where the Druj miasma is deeply rooted in the soil.
t.The Barrens: The Imperial armies and the Great Forest Orcs retreated here, and Therunin refugees found welcome among the Great Forest Orcs. Druj with tortured souls now push into Hope's Rest, while its chaos-fruit forests gain two extra fruit.
t.Therunin: Therunin fell entirely to the Druj except the vallorn regions, and most of its people fled or died. Only Peakedge Stead, the Houses of Healing and the fog-warded Thornsong House remain, while the awakened vallorn of Tharunind begins to spread.
t.Zenith: The surge of Spring magic from Therunin swept along Zenith's trods, and its chaos-fruit forests will produce two additional fruit.

r.Morrow/Altis: Pools of vallorn miasma have appeared in Altis's northern foothills, and a vallornspawn horde is moving through the valleys towards the Spire of the Canticle. The Archmage of Winter is charged with stopping it.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Pools of vallorn miasma, bringing vallornspawn and ettercaps, have been reported in Peregro's northern foothills.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Refugees from the Lower Tarn Valley fled north to the welcoming Eaves of Peytaht and the weirwood groves of the Great Forest Orcs.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: A Druj band escorting tortured souls, corrupted fallen Navarr, is advancing on the Shrine of Hope. The High Exorcist is charged with exorcising them.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: Druj forces massed here before spilling west in uncountable thousands to overrun the Tarn Valley.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The undead Iron Helms tore into the Druj here before their hunger turned indiscriminate. Imperial forces are called to destroy a Druj miasma pillar being raised in the region.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Greenheart escaped Druj conquest, but abominations stir as the vallorn wakes and its steadings are under siege. Prognosticators expect most of them to be overrun by the Summer Solstice.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The poisoned valley was evacuated and then fell swiftly to the Druj. This ended the Apothecaries' Guild's plan to cleanse it with the new antidote until the Druj are driven out.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Peakedge Song fell despite the Towerjacks' fortifications. Peakedge Stead and the Houses of Healing survive only behind Ossegrahn's temporary bramble wall, and Thornsong House is hidden in warding fog, while the vallorn's expansion is now focused here.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Sweetglades escaped Druj conquest, but its steadings are besieged as the vallorn wakes. The Lord of Thorns gathers vallornspawn there, and the Champion of Vigilance is charged with slaying it.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Defenders armed with Bloodharrow Philtre and aided by healers bought only hours before the Druj rolled over them. The region now lies in the path of the expanding vallorn.

Two suns in the sunset.d: Sufyan i Zuhri i Guerra's Loyalty mandate turned the war with the Plenum into one of survival. Three potential allies were found: the poor, martial satrapy of Ibaria, which could raise up to three armies if supplied with mithril; the reactionary Children of Asav, who would need at least 75 thrones a season; and the Lost Weepers, a dark cult wanting curse ritual texts and mana. After a League Assembly judgement, the incoming Regario Dossier could redirect spies to Asavea, but only at this summit. Donations to anchor the Way have reached 47 thrones and 14 wains of white granite but have stalled because people are confused by competing appeals. At Zemeh the Asaveans were driven off, the blockade was broken, and Sumaah pledged a dose of true liao each season.

n.Dawn: Dawnish captains such as Ursiel, Edmund Reaver and Seraphine De Sarroi took their fleets to Sumaah and fought in the victory that saved Zemeh.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the final defeat of the Druj is listed as one of several competing Imperial goals dividing public support.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean forces are said to dwarf the Grendel's, and the Plenum's warships are expected to keep bolstering the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highguard captains including Shibboleth of Tziporah's Chase and Accalon fought at Zemeh. Highguard's benefactors letting their council direct their resources is cited as an example of how future support might be organised.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orc captains Urq and Tamazi Kardak were among the fleets that fought alongside the Frieøyer to defend Zemeh.
n.Navarr: Navarr captains such as Owain Farkas and Garr helped break the Asavean assault. Navarr's call to destroy the vallorn is one of the rival appeals competing for the Empire's support.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn sent the largest contingent of captains to defend Zemeh and are helping smuggle missionaries and resources into Asavea.
n.The League: Rafael Barossa's League Assembly judgement led to the chance for the new Regario Dossier to redirect spies to Asavea. Ibarian rebel refugees are believed to have settled in the League, and League captains fought at Zemeh.
n.The Marches: Marcher captains such as Misha Kemi and Thaddeus Grimm sailed to Zemeh, where cries of "A marcher!" rang out during the battle.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sent one of the largest contingents of fleet captains, including Bron Mordssen and Káre Markusdottir, to the successful defence of Zemeh.

t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: some captains feared the Asavean fleet might instead strike the Necropolis while they waited at Sumaah.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a feared alternative Asavean target, and several captains bearing the name di Sarvos fought at Zemeh.

Unlock thy hidden gate.d: The Golden Axe, supported by the Crimson Schlacta, led the invasion. The Towerjacks and Winter Sun advanced cautiously and tried to reach the subject septs. The Citadel Guard were protected by Winter's Mantle, with their injuries passed to their allies. A Night magic ward, the Druj miasma, the Tower of the Skink garrison and three recuperating Druj armies slowed progress. Tabun nevertheless fell. Around a thousand Imperial soldiers and nearly twice as many Druj died. Lahkev could fall by Summer if nothing changes. Terrified slaves and septs shunned the Empire. Scouts found the Mirelith. Heroes could link it to the trods with Dance of Navarr and Thorn, or destroy its stones to unleash the vallorn on Bloodwater.

n.Druj: The Druj lost Tabun and much of the Bloodwater Marsh, with nearly two thousand dead, though their armies and the Tower of the Skink garrison were still fighting a war of attrition. They now face the possibility that the Empire might unleash the Bendol vallorn on their lands.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: veterans who once fought in Reikos recognised the familiar Druj miasma.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc soldiers took part in the combined campaign, and the cautious Winter Sun helped spot and break the Hidden Snake ambush at Tabun. Attempts to win over the septs and the Bloodwater Spears proved fruitless.
n.Navarr: The Mirelith offered a chance to use Dance of Navarr and Thorn to bind the Terunael stones into the trod network. This would make the trods effectively unbreakable and leave only Cavan and the severed Therunin trod still to reconnect.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard marched through Lustri under Winter's Mantle and escaped bodily harm at their allies' expense. Memories of their curses on the Salt Flats of Sanath made the slaves of the Sarangrave fear the Empire.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe, alongside the Crimson Schlacta, spearheaded the invasion, lived off the land and stormed Tabun. Without its order to take the land, the Empire would likely have made little headway.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: veterans of Ossium recognised the Druj miasma, and the rich marsh is contrasted with Ossium's harsher land.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the miasma was familiar to those who once fought the Druj in Reikos.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: the Sarangrave's slaves had heard of the terrible curses the Citadel Guard unleashed here, and veterans recognised the miasma.
t.Sarangrave: Imperial armies won a tenuous toehold in the territory, just over halfway to a beachhead, and the Citadel Guard's presence allows Imperial rituals to be cast on it. The Mirelith offers either an unbreakable trod link or a vallorn catastrophe.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: its trod was noted as recently severed, and it would be an alternative route if the vallorn blocked Bloodwater.
t.Zenith: Four Imperial armies marched through Zenith's forests to invade the Sarangrave by the Druj's old invasion route. Unleashing the vallorn could block passage between Zenith and the Sarangrave entirely.

r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard's curses during their earlier invasion of the Sydathian Fens fuelled the slaves' fear of the Empire.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The vallorn heart here is held in check by the Mirelith on its border, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction would take heroes to Mirereach on the Spring Equinox. It currently makes the region impassable to armies.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Imperial forces broke through the Night ward and the miasma and captured Tabun, and are pushing toward Lahkev with full control projected by Summer if nothing changes. Destroying the Mirelith stones could see the region swallowed by the vallorn.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: If all three Mirelith stones were destroyed, the Druj would have to pull armies back to save Nesustak Forest, and the Grynbor there would risk being wiped out.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Tower of the Skink, a massive fortification in Thornfen, sent its garrison to resist the invasion and fought at Tabun, delaying the Imperial conquest.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Whisperwood is the only onward route east once Bloodwater is taken, but a vallorn breach could block the path from Lustri and force the Druj to defend it.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The four armies marched north through Lustri's shadowed forests, where soldiers reported strange dreams and shy spirits, and the ground had grown boggy. A vallorn breach could cut Lustri off from the Sarangrave.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: the smell of the Sarangrave was likened to the Proceris marshes.

Waiting for the worms.d: Ambassador Dino i Riqueza judged that the Free Seas Pact would clash with the Liberty Pact's free trade clause, and Annike considered the required changes fatal. Several Sarcophan-linked ministries faced price rises, and the Kruidenkenner withdrew their offers, though the deBruin family kept prices steady. The Alivetti Estates prospered despite magistrates' concerns about drugs and a planned Sarcophan temple. The Lijkkever envoy Schuyler Koopman proposed a Senate appraisal for a port in Utterlund, Holberg, and offered to share its costs. House Lijkkever's entanglement in Axou politics at Issyk was being unwound. The Delves also offered to buy wains at two thrones each should market prices fall that low.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Lijkkever envoy voiced fears of the violent orcs of the 'nation of Sanath' and remained keen on a Holberg route even after learning the real nature of the Druj.
n.Highguard: A Sarcophan art dealer offering trade in stone goods with a Sarcophan sect, and a Prosperity priest warning against the deal, were due to meet Highguard benefactors at the Chapel. A Highborn egregore would hold a majority vote on accepting the offer.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the new Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, Dino i Riqueza, is of the Brass Coast, and the Madruga Municipal Docks proposal was cited as a model.
n.The League: The League saw the Alivetti Estates enclave in Sarvos prosper amid concern over drugs and a foreign temple. The Lijkkever proposed a joint port in Holberg, and the Jolly Jackdaw Cartel was named as the go-between for Wintermark investment pitches.
n.Urizen: The Pallas Docks in Urizen were completed on schedule as the deBruin Docks, protected from storms by the Ashen Flame's Summer enchantment over the south-western mountains. Their Prime Factor, Marta Kotova Novikova, would not face the price rises hitting other Sarcophan trade.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark farmers continued growing vlinderbloem for the Kraft brothers in exchange for viezesmaak. The brothers asked Winterfolk with investment schemes to pitch them through the Jolly Jackdaw Cartel.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay was described as hardly safe waters because of Asavean-backed piracy, which pushed the Lijkkever to seek a northern route instead. The deBruin family's interest in the Bay was noted as a possible opening for securing marines.
t.Holberg: The Lijkkever envoy explored Holberg and proposed that the Senate commission Naomi of Virtue's Rest to appraise a municipal port there, with costs shared in return for priority berths. Some Holbergers warned it could draw trade away from the Semmerlak.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the proposal for the Municipal Docks in Madruga was cited by the Lijkkever as the kind of outcome they hoped for in Holberg.
t.Redoubt: The redesigned Pallas Docks were completed as the deBruin Docks under the protection of the Ashen Flame's enchantment. Marta Kotova Novikova became Prime Factor, able to buy Sarcophan weirwood from the Spring Equinox.
t.Sarvos: The Sarcophan freehold at the Alivetti Estates kept prospering despite magistrates' alarm at drugs such as bite and ocean's caress, and Aaven Beekhof lingered there to sell legal narcotics. A slow-building Community of Silence temple worried the city's Vigilant.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was listed among the League cities the Lijkkever chose not to pursue trade with, given the danger in the Bay of Catazar.
t.The Semmerlak: A northern Holberg port would let foreign traders avoid crossing the haunted lake. Sceptical Holbergers warned this could harm trading posts on its shores, such as Ivarsgard Docks.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Schuyler Koopman visited the Sand Fishers in Misericorde to discuss buying lumber and weirwood from their sawmills, or hiring them to clear woodland for the proposed port.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's marshy riverbanks were explored by a Lijkkever-funded party as the proposed site of a new port, which would also need warehouses, a road to the city and defences against the Mallum.

Ward Little Boyar's Welcome.d: The motion took up an opportunity described in the Wind of Fortune "Outside the wall". The ward cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns and needed three months of work once funded. Several citizens paid for it over the year. Yakov "Yasha" Bjelovuk gave mithril and most of the money after the Spring Equinox, and Farren Silver Streams added a crown. Triska Markova gave most of the mithril across several seasons, and Nikolai Yaropolk Borislav supplied the last two wains after the Winter Solstice. Once finished, the Little Boyar's Welcome was warded against the threats of Varushka's dark powers, and the taxation of Karov rose by six thrones a season.

n.Varushka: A Varushkan fortification is now protected against the dark powers that haunt the nation's lands, paid for mostly by Varushkan citizens, and Karov's taxes have risen.

t.Karov: Karov's senator proposed the ward, and its completion raised the territory's taxation by six thrones a season.

r.Karov/Duzekani: The walls of the Little Boyar's Welcome in Duzekani are now warded against the supernatural threats of Varushka's dark powers.

What shall we do now?.d: Ilarch Maxatios thanked Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven for a storm warning but questioned continued trade across the Bay of Catazar. The Khiklotu Khrysoú did not intend to reopen trade in Therunin. Repairs at Issyk's docks stalled over a Sarcophan investor, though Imperial ships would be welcome. Kantor would now offer Sable and Blackened Key instead of orichalcum. Maxatios condemned trade in Yellow Lotus and demanded details of the pact Fintan had vaguely mentioned. Grand Ilarch Keloparia confirmed Imperial students may study art at Maykop. Dancia Terricos thanked Gabriel Barossa for his letter. Enough priests took part that Solokha was secured, a diplomatic success, though no list of visitors could be compiled.

n.Druj: The Druj had overrun Therunin and held the popular agema Menoetius, and Axou watched the Empire's foray into the Sarangrave from Ipotavo, the citadel guarding Axos against them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel were listed among the dangers making Axou trade across the Bay of Catazar increasingly hard to justify.
n.Navarr: With Therunin lost and talk of the Navarr goading the vallorn, the Khiklotu Khrysoú did not intend to reopen trade with the Navarr even if sovereignty were restored. The Navarr Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven also faced Axou irritation over his vague pact remarks.
n.The League: Former League general Gabriel Barossa received formal thanks from Dancia Terricos of Ipotavo for his letter, and League plays were said to be in demand in Issyk, where troupes were welcome to visit.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Axou had been warned of storms in the Urizen territory of Redoubt raised by the Children of Wrecks.

t.Bay of Catazar: Storms, the Grendel, the Children of Wrecks and an Asavean bounty made Axou merchants question continuing their risky trade across the bay, and Maxatios sought reassurance the problems would be dealt with.
t.Redoubt: The Imperial Ambassador's warning about storms in Redoubt raised by the Children of Wrecks prompted Axou concern about the safety of their trade routes.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: news of the Empire's foray into the Sarangrave reached Ipotavo, the citadel that guards Axos against the Druj.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Axos once tried to invade Spiral in retaliation for the fall of Solokha, which they blamed on the Empire.
t.Therunin: With the Druj overrunning Therunin and all Imperial forces withdrawn, the Khiklotu Khrysoú traders, who escaped being trapped at Peakedge Stead, did not intend to reopen their trading post there.

Wish you were here.d: The Fellowship of Purple Sails planned a nautical festival and lobbied the Fleetmaster for a new maritime sodality. Hamish, apprentice to Wind Lord Morath, landed at Sarvos under parley to meet Vossk and the Ambassador to the Grendel. The Stzena of Tears, who had spread an ominous ballad through Weirwater, came with a plaguewulf, possibly Dravec the Hunter, to speak with Varushkans. Others included a go-between for Holberg's Kleists, Kaisa of the Sewn Tongue inviting five to meet the Falconer, a Ketsov representative, trappers with a caged beast, Beoraidh's Diamant Drakes, Urizeni Stargazers, Ferozi corsairs, and Great Forest Orcs. Some herb garden owners suffered dreams of being hunted.

n.Dawn: The Stzena's Ballad of Leohanr Gildaryn, which mocks Weirwater's protector, was taken up by Dawnish singers. Charlie Stinger and the Diamant Drakes both planned to call at the Dawnish camp.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Stzena's ballad recalls Ser Emrys dying alone after fighting the Druj.
n.Grendel: Hamish, apprentice to the Wind Lord Morath, came under a flag of parley to speak privately with Vossk and the Ambassador to the Grendel. The Ferozi corsairs also wanted to discuss what the Grendel intervention over Feroz meant.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn benefactors helped found the Fellowship of Purple Sails, and citizens of Bastion and Casinea encountered some of the visitors.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Bal Blueraven stayed near Pakaanan's Pass even after Skarsind was granted to the Imperial Orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun breaking Pakaanan's Pass may have prompted Bal Blueraven to leave their hermitage.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr messenger carried Kaisa's invitation, and Navarr had facilitated the earlier meeting between the Great Forest Orcs and Wintermark.
n.The League: League merchants co-founded the Fellowship of Purple Sails, a go-between sought the Kleists of Holberg in the League camp, and the Diamant Drakes planned to visit the League first. Some League herb garden owners were troubled by hunting dreams.
n.The Marches: Beetle-studier Charlie Stinger sought romantic counsel, and Friar Aube Warren of Upwold came to the Marcher camp to discuss loyalty and the Silver Chase with Kennett the Mummer.
n.Urizen: Urizeni Stargazers headed for the Urizen camp to share celestial revelations with the Astral Arcanist Serenus Starsong, while Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was sought by the Grendel envoy.
n.Varushka: The Stzena of Tears came to negotiate on patronage with Varushka's senators, and the plaguewulf wished to speak with its wise ones about a ceremony to Zoria. A Ketsov representative also briefed prospective Burghers of Ketsov, and some Varushkan herb garden owners suffered hunting dreams.
n.Wintermark: Great Forest Orcs came to share stories with Wintermark and to discuss helping defend Kallavesa. A Kallavesi hermit sought Derowen of the Forge, and the possibly Wintermark Kaisa of the Sewn Tongue issued an invitation to meet the Falconer.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Bastion were surprised to see the purple-and-pink clad Beoraidh orcs travelling through.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Oligu Predborvana Ketsov had stayed in Casinea for two months awaiting the summit.
t.Feroz: The Wisdom sect Sular's Spyglass was based in Feroz, and the Malazine corsair siblings, who stayed behind after the evacuation, sought fellow Ferozi corsairs to discuss the Wharfage in Oran and the Grendel intervention.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's statement welcomed the Great Forest Orcs who had settled in Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the go-between Etienne di Sarvos sought representatives of the Holberg luminaries Lula and Bernhard Kleist on what may be building work.
t.Kallavesa: The Great Forest Orcs hoped to discuss how they might eventually help with Kallavesa's defences, and the hermit-artisan Bal Blueraven was Kallavesi.
t.Mareave: Orcs of the Diamant Drakes, now residents of independent Beoraidh in Mareave, travelled north seeking business connections in the Empire.
t.Ossium: A representative of the Ketsov family of Ossium came to brief candidates for Burgher of Ketsov on her family's current difficulties and hopes for the title.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Redoubt saw the Beoraidh orcs wandering through.
t.Sarvos: A Grendel ship under a flag of parley landed the envoy Hamish at the docks of Sarvos, where magistrates confirmed his safe passage under Imperial law before letting him go under watch.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Bal Blueraven spent part of each year in Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: The hermit Bal Blueraven, who stayed near Pakaanan's Pass after Skarsind went to the Imperial Orcs, left for Anvil once the pass was reopened.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: citizens of Spiral saw the Beoraidh orcs on their travels.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Savra and the Great Forest Orcs were weary after their retreat from Therunin.
t.Upwold: Friar Aube Warren, one of Upwold's great listeners, set out with a member of their community to discuss loyalty and the Silver Chase.
t.Weirwater: The Stzena of Tears demanded hospitality from travellers in northern Weirwater, spreading a ballad mocking the province's protector and saying it would not be safe from husks.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was one of those the Grendel envoy asked to meet.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The independent city of Beoraidh sent members of the Diamant Drakes, a gambling and gladiator venture, to forge closer ties with its northern neighbours.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Bal Blueraven left their hidden hermitage in the hills above Pakaanan's Pass after the Jotun broke the pass and it reopened.
